courses.title: English Language Arts 6
courses.description: Grade 6 ELA builds close reading of literature and nonfiction, evidence-based writing in all three types (narrative, explanatory, argument), and middle-school grammar and vocabulary. Students read classic short stories, the survival novel Hatchet, Greek myths and the Odyssey, poetry, Helen Keller's autobiography, a Shakespeare comedy and The Secret Garden, then finish with a research project. Grammar (pronouns, punctuation of nonrestrictive elements, sentence variety), Greek and Latin roots, and speaking and listening are woven into every week.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts/Literacy; 2014 CA ELA/ELD Framework

standards.RL.6.1: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what a literary text says explicitly and by inference.
standards.RL.6.2: Determine a theme or central idea and how it is conveyed through details; summarize without personal opinions.
standards.RL.6.3: Describe how a plot unfolds in episodes and how characters respond or change as the plot moves toward resolution.
standards.RL.6.4: Determine meanings of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze impact of word choice on meaning and tone.
standards.RL.6.5: Analyze how a sentence, chapter, scene or stanza fits into the overall structure and contributes to theme, setting or plot.
standards.RL.6.6: Explain how an author develops the point of view of the narrator or speaker.
standards.RL.6.7: Compare and contrast reading a story, drama or poem with listening to or viewing an audio, video or live version.
standards.RL.6.9: Compare and contrast texts in different forms or genres in terms of their approaches to similar themes and topics.
standards.RL.6.10: Read and comprehend grade 6-8 literature, including stories, dramas and poems, proficiently.
standards.RI.6.1: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what an informational text says explicitly and by inference.
standards.RI.6.2: Determine a central idea and how it is conveyed through details; provide an objective summary.
standards.RI.6.3: Analyze how a key individual, event or idea is introduced, illustrated and elaborated in a text.
standards.RI.6.4: Determine meanings of words and phrases in informational text, including figurative, connotative and technical meanings.
standards.RI.6.5: Analyze how a sentence, paragraph, chapter or section fits into the overall structure of a text.
standards.RI.6.6: Determine an author's point of view or purpose and explain how it is conveyed.
standards.RI.6.7: Integrate information presented in different media or formats as well as in words.
standards.RI.6.8: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing supported from unsupported claims.
standards.RI.6.9: Compare and contrast one author's presentation of events with that of another (e.g., memoir vs. biography).
standards.RI.6.10: Read and comprehend grade 6-8 literary nonfiction proficiently.
standards.W.6.1: Write arguments supporting claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
standards.W.6.2: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas through relevant content.
standards.W.6.3: Write narratives developing real or imagined experiences using effective technique, descriptive details and well-structured event sequences.
standards.W.6.4: Produce clear and coherent writing appropriate to task, purpose and audience.
standards.W.6.5: Develop and strengthen writing by planning, revising, editing, rewriting or trying a new approach.
standards.W.6.6: Use technology to produce and publish writing and to interact with others; type a minimum of three pages in one sitting.
standards.W.6.7: Conduct short research projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing as appropriate.
standards.W.6.8: Gather relevant information from print and digital sources, assess credibility, quote or paraphrase, and provide bibliographic information.
standards.W.6.9: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection and research.
standards.W.6.10: Write routinely over extended and shorter time frames for a range of tasks and purposes.
standards.SL.6.1: Engage effectively in collaborative discussions, building on others' ideas and expressing one's own clearly.
standards.SL.6.2: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats and explain how it contributes to a topic.
standards.SL.6.3: Delineate a speaker's argument and claims, distinguishing supported from unsupported claims.
standards.SL.6.4: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically with pertinent details; use appropriate eye contact, volume and pronunciation.
standards.SL.6.5: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.
standards.SL.6.6: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when appropriate.
standards.L.6.1: Demonstrate command of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.
standards.L.6.1a: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).
standards.L.6.1c: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.
standards.L.6.1d: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (unclear or ambiguous antecedents).
standards.L.6.1e: Recognize variations from standard English in writing and speaking and use strategies to improve expression.
standards.L.6.2: Demonstrate command of capitalization, punctuation and spelling when writing.
standards.L.6.2a: Use commas, parentheses or dashes to set off nonrestrictive or parenthetical elements.
standards.L.6.3: Use knowledge of language and its conventions; vary sentence patterns for meaning, interest and style; maintain consistency in style and tone.
standards.L.6.4: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown words using context, affixes and roots, and reference materials.
standards.L.6.4b: Use common grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to meaning (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).
standards.L.6.5: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships and nuances in word meanings (personification, connotation).
standards.L.6.6: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases.

units.title: Short Stories and Personal Narrative
units.big_idea: Authors build plot, character and suspense through deliberate choices we can imitate in our own narratives.

units.title: Survival: Hatchet Novel Study
units.big_idea: Facing adversity changes people; fiction and nonfiction together show how humans survive.

units.title: Myths, Heroes and the Odyssey
units.big_idea: Ancient myths and epics carry themes about courage, pride and home that still shape our language and stories.

units.title: Argument: Claims and Evidence
units.big_idea: Strong arguments make clear claims supported by relevant, credible evidence and fair reasoning.

units.title: Poetry: Sound, Image and Meaning
units.big_idea: Poets compress meaning into images, sounds and structure; figurative language shapes tone.

units.title: Memoir and Biography: Helen Keller
units.big_idea: Writers of memoir shape their own story; comparing memoir and biography reveals point of view.

units.title: Drama: A Midsummer Night's Dream
units.big_idea: Plays are written to be performed; staging, voice and movement bring the text's comedy and conflict to life.

units.title: Novel Study: The Secret Garden
units.big_idea: Characters and settings can transform together; a theme emerges from how characters change.

units.title: Research and Presentation
units.big_idea: Researchers ask focused questions, evaluate sources, synthesize information and share it clearly.

objectives: Map the plot structure of a short story
materials: 'Rikki-Tikki-Tavi' by Rudyard Kipling (from The Jungle Book)

days.title: Reader's notebook launch
days.work: Set up a reader's notebook, write a reading-history page, and read the first third of 'Rikki-Tikki-Tavi', jotting predictions about the cobras.

days.title: Character and evidence
days.work: Finish the story; list three traits of Rikki with a quoted line of evidence for each, and practice the 'claim + quote + explain' paragraph frame.

days.title: Plot mountain
days.work: Draw a plot diagram of the story and mark where Kipling builds suspense; discuss with a parent which moment is the climax and why.

days.title: Pronoun case
days.work: Lesson on subjective, objective and possessive pronouns; correct 15 sentences (e.g., 'Him and me went') and find 5 pronouns in the story.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a one-paragraph response explaining how Rikki changes from beginning to end, citing two quotations; take a 10-item pronoun-case quiz.

weeks.assessment: Evidence paragraph on character plus pronoun-case quiz.

weeks.topic: Irony and point of view: O. Henry and Saki
objectives: Explain how narration affects what readers know
materials: 'The Ransom of Red Chief' and 'After Twenty Years' by O. Henry

days.title: Situational irony
days.work: Read 'The Ransom of Red Chief' and chart what the kidnappers expect vs. what happens; write two sentences explaining the irony.

days.title: Narrator's voice
days.work: Analyze how Sam's first-person narration and fancy vocabulary create humor; rewrite one paragraph in plain third person and compare the effect.

days.title: Twist endings
days.work: Read 'After Twenty Years' and 'The Open Window'; mark foreshadowing clues on a second read and discuss which twist was fairer to the reader.

days.title: Context clues
days.work: Use context clues to define 10 challenging words from the O. Henry stories, then verify with a dictionary.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short comparison of how two of the three stories use point of view to surprise readers; quiz on irony and pronoun case.

objectives: Plan a personal narrative around a meaningful moment
Use dialogue, pacing and sensory detail

days.title: Finding a story
days.work: Brainstorm a heart map of memorable moments, choose one small moment, and tell it aloud to a listener in two minutes.

days.title: Strong leads
days.work: Study leads from the unit's stories and write three possible openings for your narrative (action, dialogue, setting).

days.title: Drafting with dialogue
days.work: Draft the middle of your narrative, including at least four lines of correctly punctuated dialogue.

days.title: Slow-motion moment
days.work: Expand the most important moment with sensory detail and inner thoughts so it takes up at least a full paragraph.

days.title: Ending and reflection
days.work: Draft an ending that reflects on why the moment mattered and read the full draft aloud for a family member's feedback.

weeks.assessment: Complete draft checked against a narrative checklist.

objectives: Revise for sentence variety and word choice
Edit for pronoun use and punctuation

days.title: Sentence variety
days.work: Lesson on varying sentence beginnings and lengths; revise ten sentences in your draft so no two consecutive sentences start the same way.

days.title: Word choice
days.work: Replace weak verbs and vague nouns with precise ones; highlight five improvements in a different color.

days.title: Editing conference
days.work: Edit with a checklist for pronoun case, dialogue punctuation, capitalization and spelling, then conference with a parent.

days.title: Publish
days.work: Type the final narrative (at least 2 pages) and add a title.

days.title: Author's chair and check
days.work: Read your narrative aloud with expression to an audience and score it with the narrative rubric; take a unit vocabulary quiz.

weeks.assessment: Published personal narrative scored on a 4-point rubric.

days.title: Before the crash
days.work: Read chapter 1, locate the flight route on a map of Canada, and note what we learn about Brian and the Secret.

days.title: Crash landing
days.work: Read chapters 2-3; list sensory words Paulsen uses during the crash and explain how short sentences build tension.

days.title: First night
days.work: Read chapter 4; make a T-chart of Brian's physical and emotional problems and discuss which is worse.

days.title: Intensive pronouns
days.work: Lesson on intensive pronouns (himself, myself); write 8 sentences about Brian using them correctly and fix 6 misuse errors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Reading check quiz on chapters 1-4 and a journal entry from Brian's point of view after the first night.

weeks.assessment: Reading quiz and point-of-view journal entry.

objectives: Read informational text on survival priorities
materials: ReadWorks or CommonLit wilderness survival article

days.title: Shelter and food
days.work: Read chapters 5-6 and list Brian's survival decisions with page numbers; rate each decision smart or risky.

days.title: Self-pity
days.work: Read chapters 7-8; write a paragraph explaining Brian's lesson that self-pity 'didn't work', citing two quotes.

days.title: Fire
days.work: Read chapter 9 and annotate how Paulsen describes fire as a 'friend'; identify personification.

days.title: Survival nonfiction
days.work: Read a wilderness-survival article and the Ten Essentials list, then summarize the central idea objectively in 4-5 sentences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare Brian's priorities with the article's advice in a Venn diagram and take a chapters 5-9 reading quiz.

days.title: Foolbirds and fish
days.work: Read chapters 10-11 and record what Brian learns from failure while hunting; connect to the idea of 'tough hope'.

days.title: The plane passes
days.work: Read chapter 12 and write a journal entry analyzing how the missed rescue plane is a turning point.

days.title: New Brian
days.work: Read chapter 13 and complete a 'Brian then vs. now' character-change chart with evidence.

days.title: Pronoun shifts
days.work: Lesson on shifts in pronoun number and person; correct 12 sentences such as 'If a person gets lost, you should stay calm'.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draft a theme statement for Hatchet (not just a topic word) and support it with three details; quiz on chapters 10-13.

days.title: The moose and the tornado
days.work: Read chapters 14-15 and explain how these setbacks test the 'new Brian'.

days.title: Back to the plane
days.work: Read chapters 16-17; list the items in the survival pack and predict how they will change his life.

days.title: Rescue
days.work: Read chapters 18-19 and the epilogue; discuss how the epilogue changes our understanding of the story's ending.

days.title: Listen and compare
days.work: Listen to a chapter of the audiobook while following along and note what the narrator's voice adds or changes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the final Hatchet comprehension test with short constructed responses.

objectives: Write an explanatory essay with evidence from fiction and nonfiction

days.title: Thesis and plan
days.work: Write a thesis explaining three ways Brian survives (mental and physical) and fill an essay organizer with evidence.

days.title: Body paragraphs
days.work: Draft three body paragraphs, each with a quote from Hatchet and one fact from the survival article.

days.title: Intro and conclusion
days.work: Draft an introduction with a hook and a conclusion that explains what Brian's survival teaches readers.

days.title: Revise and edit
days.work: Revise for transitions and precise words; edit for pronoun shifts and intensive pronouns, then type the final essay.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Submit the essay, self-score with the explanatory rubric, and take the unit vocabulary test.

weeks.assessment: Explanatory essay scored on rubric; vocabulary test.

objectives: Use Greek and Latin roots to determine meaning
materials: 'A Wonder-Book' and 'Tanglewood Tales' by Nathaniel Hawthorne (Project Gutenberg)
D'Aulaires' Book of Greek Myths (library, optional)

days.title: Why myths?
days.work: Read the myth of Prometheus and list what it explains (fire, human suffering); discuss why cultures created myths.

days.title: Pandora's box
days.work: Read Hawthorne's 'The Paradise of Children' (Pandora) and write the theme in one sentence with supporting evidence.

days.title: Midas and hubris
days.work: Read 'The Golden Touch' (King Midas) and analyze how Midas's choices drive the plot to its resolution.

days.title: Words from myths
days.work: Study roots and words from myths (narcissist, echo, panic, tantalize, chronology, psyche) and build a 20-word root map.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on myth themes and roots; retell a myth orally to a family member in two minutes.

materials: 'The Children's Homer' by Padraic Colum (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Meet Odysseus
days.work: Read the opening of the Odysseus section of The Children's Homer, map the start of his journey, and list epic hero traits.

days.title: The Cyclops
days.work: Read the Polyphemus episode and cite evidence that Odysseus is both clever and proud.

days.title: Aeolus and Circe
days.work: Read the bag of winds and Circe episodes and explain how the crew's choices cause new problems.

days.title: Root review
days.work: Find 10 words in the reading with Greek or Latin parts (e.g., 'journey', 'monstrous') and analyze them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph analyzing which episode best shows Odysseus's greatest flaw; reading quiz.

objectives: Compare text with a film or audio version
materials: audio or animated clip of the Sirens episode

days.title: Sirens, Scylla and Charybdis
days.work: Read the Sirens and Scylla episodes and discuss what they suggest about temptation and leadership.

days.title: Return to Ithaca
days.work: Read Odysseus's return in disguise and trace how Penelope tests him.

days.title: Themes across the epic
days.work: Write two theme statements for the Odyssey (e.g., about loyalty or pride) with evidence.

days.title: Text vs. media
days.work: Watch or listen to a retelling of the Sirens episode and compare it with the text in a chart of what was added, cut or changed.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a comparison of how a Greek myth and the Odyssey both treat pride (RL.6.9) and take the Odyssey quiz.

weeks.topic: Writing: modern myth or hero's journey story
objectives: Write a narrative using hero's-journey structure
Use precise language and transitions to show time shifts

days.title: Hero's journey
days.work: Map Odysseus's and Brian's stories onto the hero's journey and plan your own hero's journey story or modern myth.

days.title: Draft beginning
days.work: Draft your story's opening and call to adventure using vivid setting details.

days.title: Draft trials
days.work: Draft two trials your hero faces, using dialogue and transitions that show time shifts.

days.title: Revise and edit
days.work: Revise the climax and return; edit for pronoun case and consistent verb tense, then type the final draft.

days.title: Share and check
days.work: Read your story aloud and score it with the narrative rubric; take the unit test on myths and the Odyssey.

weeks.assessment: Narrative scored on rubric; unit test.

materials: CommonLit argument articles (e.g., on school start times, homework, screen time)

days.title: What is an argument?
days.work: Compare a fact, an opinion and an argument; identify the claim in 6 short advertisements and op-ed excerpts.

days.title: Claim, reasons, evidence
days.work: Read an article on whether middle schools should start later and annotate the claim, reasons and evidence in three colors.

days.title: Supported or not?
days.work: Evaluate each piece of evidence in a second article as relevant, sufficient or unsupported and explain why.

days.title: Author's purpose and bias
days.work: Determine each author's point of view and identify loaded words that reveal bias.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read a new short argument and complete an argument-analysis organizer independently as a quiz.

objectives: Write a clear claim and gather evidence
materials: two to three articles on a chosen issue (e.g., Should zoos exist? Should kids have phones?)

days.title: Choose a question
days.work: Choose a debatable question from a list, read two articles on it, and take a position.

days.title: Evidence notes
days.work: Take notes on cards, separating quotations and paraphrases, with source titles.

days.title: Vague pronouns
days.work: Lesson on vague pronouns ('they say', 'this'); fix 12 sentences with unclear antecedents.

days.title: Outline
days.work: Outline an essay with a claim, two or three reasons, evidence for each and a counterclaim with rebuttal.

days.title: Check-in
days.work: Explain your outline orally to a parent in 3 minutes and revise based on their questions; quiz on vague pronouns.

objectives: Draft an argument essay with formal style

days.title: Introduction
days.work: Draft an introduction with a hook, background and a precise claim.

days.title: Body paragraphs
days.work: Draft body paragraphs that explain how each piece of evidence supports your reason.

days.title: Counterclaim
days.work: Draft a counterclaim-and-rebuttal paragraph and a conclusion that follows from the argument.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise for formal style (no slang, no 'I think') and add transitions like 'furthermore' and 'however'.

days.title: Edit and publish
days.work: Edit for pronoun use, commas and spelling and type the final essay; self-score with the argument rubric.

materials: a recorded student speech or TED-Ed talk

days.title: Evaluate a speech
days.work: Watch a short persuasive speech and note the speaker's claims and whether each is supported.

days.title: Prepare a speech
days.work: Turn your essay into a 2-minute opening statement with note cards.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Practice delivery (eye contact, volume, pace) while recording yourself and critique the video.

days.title: Debate
days.work: Hold a structured debate with a family member or co-op partner: opening statements, rebuttals and closings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a reflection on the debate and take the unit test on argument terms and analysis.

weeks.assessment: Debate performance rubric and unit test.

objectives: Identify simile, metaphor, personification and hyperbole
Explain how figurative language affects meaning
materials: 'Hope is the thing with feathers' by Emily Dickinson

days.title: Images
days.work: Read 'Fog' and sketch the image it creates; identify the metaphor and explain what it suggests about fog.

days.title: Extended metaphor
days.work: Read Dickinson's 'Hope is the thing with feathers' and annotate each stanza's development of the bird metaphor.

days.title: Hughes's dreams
days.work: Read Hughes's 'Dreams' and 'Mother to Son'; compare their metaphors and tones.

days.title: Connotation
days.work: Sort word pairs by connotation (thrifty/stingy, slender/skinny) and rewrite a stanza changing connotations to alter tone.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write your own poem using an extended metaphor; quiz on figurative language identification.

weeks.assessment: Figurative language quiz and original poem.

objectives: Explain how stanza structure contributes to meaning
materials: 'Paul Revere's Ride' by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Read 'Paul Revere's Ride' aloud and tap the galloping meter; explain how rhythm matches content.

days.title: Rhyme scheme
days.work: Label rhyme schemes of three poems and identify alliteration and internal rhyme in an excerpt of 'The Raven'.

days.title: Heard vs. read
days.work: Listen to a professional recording of 'The Raven' excerpt and compare it with your silent reading.

days.title: Structure
days.work: Analyze how one stanza of 'Paul Revere's Ride' builds suspense within the whole poem.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Memorize and recite 12+ lines of a chosen poem with expression; quiz on sound devices.

materials: 'The Road Not Taken' by Robert Frost
'Who Has Seen the Wind?' by Christina Rossetti
'The Land of Counterpane' by Robert Louis Stevenson

days.title: The speaker
days.work: Read 'The Road Not Taken' and describe the speaker's situation and attitude with evidence.

days.title: Theme in Frost
days.work: Debate the poem's theme (is it really about choosing the 'less traveled' road?) and write a theme paragraph.

days.title: Tone words
days.work: Read Rossetti and Stevenson poems, choose precise tone words for each, and cite the lines that create that tone.

days.title: Free verse
days.work: Read a free-verse poem from CommonLit and compare its structure with Frost's rhymed stanzas.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Analyze an unseen poem independently for speaker, tone and theme as a quiz.

days.title: Ode
days.work: Write an ode to an ordinary object using at least three types of figurative language.

days.title: Haiku and concrete poems
days.work: Write three haiku about nature observations and one concrete (shape) poem.

days.title: Narrative poem
days.work: Write a short narrative poem with a rhyme scheme, modeled on Longfellow.

days.title: Compile
days.work: Revise and compile 6-8 poems into an illustrated anthology with a table of contents and author's note.

days.title: Poetry cafe
days.work: Host a family poetry reading performing three poems; take the unit test on poetry terms.

weeks.assessment: Anthology rubric, performance and unit test.

weeks.topic: The Story of My Life, chapters 1-4
objectives: Determine how an author introduces key ideas and events
Analyze point of view in autobiography
materials: 'The Story of My Life' by Helen Keller (Project Gutenberg)

days.title: Early childhood
days.work: Read chapters 1-2 and list how Keller introduces her illness and frustrations; note how the adult Keller looks back on her child self.

days.title: The 'water' moment
days.work: Read chapters 3-4 and analyze the water-pump moment: how does Keller's word choice show it was life-changing?

days.title: Commas, parentheses, dashes
days.work: Lesson on setting off nonrestrictive and parenthetical elements; punctuate 15 sentences about Keller three ways and discuss the effect.

days.title: Point of view
days.work: Write a paragraph on Keller's purpose in writing her autobiography, with two quotations.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Reading quiz on chapters 1-4 and punctuation quiz.

weeks.topic: The Story of My Life, selected chapters 5-23
objectives: Trace the development of a central idea

days.title: Learning language
days.work: Read chapters 5-7 and trace how Anne Sullivan teaches Keller, listing each method.

days.title: Braille and reading
days.work: Read about Keller learning to read and write; use a Braille chart to write your name with glue dots on cardstock.

days.title: Learning to speak
days.work: Read chapter 13 on learning to speak and explain how this section contributes to the central idea.

days.title: Objective summary
days.work: Write a 150-word objective summary of the selections read so far.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on central idea and structure; discuss with a parent what surprised you most.

objectives: Compare how different authors present the same events
Compare text with a filmed or staged version
materials: a children's biography of Helen Keller (library)
film clip of the water-pump scene from 'The Miracle Worker' (1962)

days.title: Biography account
days.work: Read a biography's account of the water-pump scene and annotate differences from Keller's own account.

days.title: Compare authors
days.work: Complete a comparison chart: what each author includes, omits and emphasizes, and why.

days.title: Film scene
days.work: Watch the water-pump scene from 'The Miracle Worker' and note how actors, sound and camera change the experience.

days.title: Primary sources
days.work: Look at Library of Congress photographs and letters related to Helen Keller and explain what they add.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a 3-paragraph comparison of memoir vs. biography vs. film versions of the same event.

objectives: Write a memoir chapter about a time you learned something hard

days.title: Plan
days.work: Brainstorm moments when you learned something difficult and plan a memoir chapter with a turning point.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Draft the chapter, combining narration of events with adult-like reflection, as Keller does.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise for voice and add at least three nonrestrictive elements punctuated with commas, parentheses or dashes.

days.title: Edit and publish
days.work: Edit for conventions and publish the chapter typed.

days.title: Share and check
days.work: Read your chapter aloud and take the unit test on informational reading skills.

weeks.topic: Shakespeare's world and A Midsummer Night's Dream, Act 1-2
materials: 'Tales from Shakespeare' by Charles and Mary Lamb (Project Gutenberg)
Folger Shakespeare text of A Midsummer Night's Dream (free online)

days.title: Shakespeare's theater
days.work: Learn about the Globe Theatre and Elizabethan stage; read the Lambs' prose retelling of the play for an overview.

days.work: Take a comprehension quiz and write a short analysis of how one scene contributes to the play's comedy.

objectives: Perform a scene with appropriate voice and movement
Compare live or filmed performance to the text

days.title: View a performance

days.title: Colin's tantrum

days.title: Into the garden

days.title: Magic

days.title: Homecoming

days.title: Review & check

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics 6
courses.description: Grade 6 math moves from whole-number arithmetic toward algebraic thinking. Students reason with ratios, rates and percents, complete their understanding of division with fractions, extend the number system to negative rational numbers, write and solve one-variable equations, find area, surface area and volume, and begin statistics by describing distributions. The sequence follows the Illustrative Mathematics / Open Up Resources Grade 6 scope used by many California districts.
courses.framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics; 2023 CA Mathematics Framework

standards.6.RP.A.1: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a relationship between two quantities.
standards.6.RP.A.2: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b (b not 0) and use rate language.
standards.6.RP.A.3: Use ratio and rate reasoning (tables, tape diagrams, double number lines, equations) to solve real-world problems.
standards.6.RP.A.3a: Make tables of equivalent ratios, find missing values, plot pairs on the coordinate plane, and compare ratios.
standards.6.RP.A.3b: Solve unit rate problems, including unit pricing and constant speed.
standards.6.RP.A.3c: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100; solve problems finding the whole given a part and the percent.
standards.6.RP.A.3d: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; transform units when multiplying or dividing quantities.
standards.6.NS.A.1: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.
standards.6.NS.B.2: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.
standards.6.NS.B.3: Fluently add, subtract, multiply and divide multi-digit decimals using standard algorithms.
standards.6.NS.B.4: Find the greatest common factor (to 100) and least common multiple (to 12); use the distributive property to factor sums.
standards.6.NS.C.5: Use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts and explain the meaning of 0.
standards.6.NS.C.6: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line; extend number lines and coordinate axes to negative numbers.
standards.6.NS.C.6c: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a number line and coordinate plane.
standards.6.NS.C.7: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.
standards.6.NS.C.8: Solve real-world problems by graphing points in all four quadrants, including distances between points sharing a coordinate.
standards.6.EE.A.1: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.
standards.6.EE.A.2: Write, read and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.
standards.6.EE.A.2c: Evaluate expressions and formulas (e.g., V = s^3, A = 6s^2) at specific values using order of operations.
standards.6.EE.A.3: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.
standards.6.EE.A.4: Identify when two expressions are equivalent.
standards.6.EE.B.5: Understand solving an equation or inequality as finding which values make it true; use substitution to check.
standards.6.EE.B.6: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving real-world problems.
standards.6.EE.B.7: Solve real-world problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for nonnegative rational numbers.
standards.6.EE.B.8: Write inequalities of the form x > c or x < c for real-world constraints and represent solutions on number lines.
standards.6.EE.C.9: Use variables to represent two quantities that change together; relate dependent and independent variables with tables, graphs and equations.
standards.6.G.A.1: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons by composing and decomposing shapes.
standards.6.G.A.2: Find the volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths; apply V = lwh and V = bh.
standards.6.G.A.3: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given vertices; use coordinates to find side lengths.
standards.6.G.A.4: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets of rectangles and triangles and use nets to find surface area.
standards.6.SP.A.1: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data.
standards.6.SP.A.2: Understand that a data distribution can be described by its center, spread and overall shape.
standards.6.SP.A.3: Recognize that a measure of center summarizes all values with one number, while a measure of variation describes how values vary.
standards.6.SP.B.4: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms and box plots.
standards.6.SP.B.5: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context (count, attribute measured, center and variability, shape, outliers).
standards.MP.1: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
standards.MP.3: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

units.title: Area and Surface Area
units.big_idea: Area can be found by cutting, rearranging and decomposing shapes; surface area is the total area of a solid's faces.

units.title: Introducing Ratios
units.big_idea: A ratio compares two quantities, and equivalent ratios describe the same relationship at different scales.

units.title: Unit Rates and Percentages
units.big_idea: Unit rates and percents (rates per 100) let us compare and convert quantities efficiently.

units.title: Dividing Fractions
units.big_idea: Division asks 'how many groups?' or 'how much in each group?', and those questions work for fractions too.

units.title: Arithmetic in Base Ten
units.big_idea: Place value makes the standard algorithms for decimals and long division work.

units.title: Expressions and Equations
units.big_idea: Variables let us write general relationships, find unknowns and show how one quantity depends on another.

units.title: Rational Numbers
units.big_idea: Negative numbers extend the number line and the coordinate plane to describe opposite directions and values below zero.

units.title: Data Sets and Distributions
units.big_idea: Statistical questions expect variability; we describe a distribution by its center, spread and shape.

units.title: Putting It All Together
units.big_idea: The year's tools combine to model real situations.

objectives: Find area by decomposing and rearranging
Derive and use A = bh for parallelograms

days.title: Tiling the plane
days.work: Compare areas of tangram shapes by covering them with smaller pieces, then explain in writing why two different-looking shapes can have equal area.

days.title: Composing and decomposing
days.work: Find the area of L-shaped and staircase regions on graph paper three different ways (cut apart, enclose and subtract, rearrange) and record each method.

days.title: Parallelograms to rectangles
days.work: Cut a paper parallelogram along its height, slide the triangle to form a rectangle, and use this to write A = b x h; solve 8 parallelogram area problems.

days.title: Bases and heights
days.work: Identify every base-height pair on tilted parallelograms, including heights that fall outside the shape, and compute areas of 10 drawn figures.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 10-problem quiz on rectangle and parallelogram area and write one sentence correcting any error you made.

weeks.assessment: Quiz: area of composite rectangles and parallelograms; explanation of why A = bh works.

objectives: Derive A = 1/2 bh from two copies of a triangle
Find any base and height of a triangle

days.title: Two copies make a parallelogram
days.work: Trace and cut two identical triangles, join them into a parallelogram, and explain why a triangle's area is half of b x h.

days.title: Right triangles
days.work: Find areas of 10 right triangles on a grid and write a rule using the two legs as base and height.

days.title: Any base, any height
days.work: For acute and obtuse triangles, draw all three heights with a ruler and show the area comes out the same using each base.

days.title: Triangle formula practice
days.work: Solve 12 triangle-area problems including missing-base and missing-height problems (e.g., area 24 sq cm and base 8 cm; find height).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz mixing triangle and parallelogram area, then correct mistakes and explain one in a short paragraph.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on triangle area including finding missing dimensions.

objectives: Find area of trapezoids and other polygons by decomposing

days.title: Decomposing polygons
days.work: Split a trapezoid, a kite and a pentagon into triangles and rectangles and find each area; compare two different decompositions.

days.title: Trapezoid strategies
days.work: Use two copies of a trapezoid to make a parallelogram and solve 8 trapezoid-area problems with your own reasoning.

days.title: Measure a room
days.work: Measure a room or yard at home, sketch it to scale on graph paper, and calculate its area in square feet.

days.title: Covering a surface
days.work: Determine how many 1 ft square tiles and how many boxes of tiles (10 per box) would cover the room you measured, including irregular parts.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 6-problem composite-figure assessment and present your floor plan calculation to a family member.

weeks.assessment: Composite polygon quiz plus floor-plan area project.

weeks.topic: Nets, surface area, squares and cubes
objectives: Draw nets of prisms and pyramids
Write s^2 and s^3 with exponents

days.title: Polyhedra and faces
days.work: Sort household objects into prisms and pyramids, count faces, edges and vertices, and record them in a table.

days.title: Unfold a box
days.work: Cut open a cereal box along its edges to make a net, measure each face and compute its surface area; compare with a partner's or parent's estimate.

days.title: Nets to surface area
days.work: Draw nets for a cube, a rectangular prism and a square pyramid on grid paper, fold one from cardstock, and calculate surface area of each.

days.title: Squares and cubes
days.work: Build cubes with snap cubes to model 2^3, 3^3, 4^3; write area of a square as s^2, volume of a cube as s^3, and surface area as 6s^2; evaluate for 8 side lengths.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the Unit 1 assessment (area of polygons, nets, surface area, exponent notation) and redo two missed problems with explanation.

objectives: Use ratio language a:b, a to b, a for every b

days.title: Introducing ratios
days.work: Describe collections of beans or counters with ratio language in three forms (3:2, 3 to 2, 3 for every 2) and write 10 ratio sentences.

days.title: Ratio diagrams
days.work: Draw discrete diagrams for recipe ratios (e.g., 2 cups flour for every 3 eggs) and answer which-ratio-matches questions.

days.title: Recipes and batches
days.work: Make one batch and a double batch of a drink mix (e.g., 2 scoops per 1 cup water), taste-test that they match, and explain why the ratio is equivalent.

days.title: Color mixing
days.work: Mix food coloring drops with water in 1:5 and 2:10 ratios to check that equivalent ratios make the same color; record observations in a table.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: write and interpret ratios from pictures and stories; explain the difference between a part-to-part and part-to-whole ratio.

weeks.assessment: Ratio language quiz and color-mixing lab write-up.

weeks.topic: Equivalent ratios and double number lines
objectives: Generate equivalent ratios by multiplying or dividing
Use double number lines to solve problems

days.title: Defining equivalent ratios
days.work: Generate five ratios equivalent to 3:4 by multiplying both quantities, then decide whether 6 lists of ratio pairs are equivalent.

days.title: Double number lines
days.work: Draw double number lines for a 2-mile per 30-minute walking pace and answer 6 questions about time and distance.

days.title: Price per item
days.work: Use real grocery receipts to build double number lines for cost and quantity and find the cost of 1, 5 and 12 items.

days.title: Same speed?
days.work: Time yourself walking 20 steps, then use a double number line to predict time for 60 and 100 steps; test one prediction.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a quiz on equivalent ratios and double number lines; correct errors in a different color.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on equivalent ratios and double number lines.

objectives: Graph ratio pairs on the coordinate plane

days.title: Ratio tables
days.work: Convert three double number lines into ratio tables, and fill in missing values in 8 tables using multiplication and scaling.

days.title: Tables and graphs
days.work: Plot ratio-table pairs (e.g., cups of rice to cups of water) on the first quadrant and notice that the points line up through (0,0).

days.title: Which is faster?
days.work: Compare two runners and two recipes using tables with a common row; justify which is faster or stronger in writing.

days.title: Problem solving
days.work: Solve 6 multi-step ratio word problems from Illustrative Math Grade 6 Unit 2, showing a table for each.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on completing tables, graphing ratio pairs and comparing ratios.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on ratio tables and graphs.

objectives: Use tape diagrams for part-part-whole problems

days.title: Tape diagrams
days.work: Use tape diagrams to solve 'ratio of boys to girls is 2:3 and there are 30 students' style problems (8 problems).

days.title: Trail mix lab
days.work: Make trail mix in a 3:2 nuts-to-raisins ratio for a total of 2 cups, using a tape diagram to plan amounts before measuring.

days.title: Choosing representations
days.work: Solve the same 4 problems with a table, a double number line and a tape diagram, and write which was most efficient and why.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed ratio review set covering language, equivalence, tables, graphs and tape diagrams.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the Unit 2 end-of-unit assessment and write a reflection on the strategy you rely on most.

weeks.topic: Units of measure and unit rates
objectives: Find and interpret both unit rates in a ratio
materials: measuring cups and a liter bottle

days.title: Measuring with different units
days.work: Measure the same objects in inches and centimeters and in cups and milliliters, and record why the numbers differ.

days.title: Converting units
days.work: Use the ratio 1 in : 2.54 cm and 1 ft : 12 in to convert 12 measurements with ratio tables.

days.title: Two unit rates
days.work: For 'every 4 cups of water makes 3 servings' find both unit rates (cups per serving, servings per cup) and explain when each is useful.

days.title: Rates at home
days.work: Time how many seconds it takes to fill a 1-liter bottle at the faucet and calculate liters per minute and minutes per liter.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on unit conversion and finding unit rates.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on conversions and unit rates.

objectives: Compare unit prices to find the better buy
materials: store flyer or online grocery prices

days.title: Constant speed
days.work: Solve 8 problems using distance = rate x time reasoning with tables (e.g., a cyclist at 12 miles per hour).

days.title: Speed lab
days.work: Measure a 20-meter course, time yourself walking, jogging and hopping, and compute meters per second for each.

days.title: Unit price
days.work: Compare 6 pairs of grocery items in different sizes using unit price, and decide the better buy for each.

days.title: Rate problems
days.work: Solve mixed rate problems (pages per minute, heartbeats per minute, cost per ounce) and justify one answer to a family member.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on constant speed and unit price problems.

weeks.assessment: Quiz plus speed lab data table.

objectives: Understand percent as a rate per 100
Find percents of quantities using double number lines and tables

days.title: What is a percent?
days.work: Shade 10 x 10 grids to show 25%, 40%, 7% and 120%, and connect percents to fractions and decimals out of 100.

days.title: Benchmark percents
days.work: Find 10%, 25%, 50% and 75% of 8 different quantities using mental math and double number lines.

days.title: Percent of a quantity
days.work: Use tables to find percents such as 35% of $80 and 15% of 60 minutes (10 problems).

days.title: Sales and tips
days.work: Calculate sale prices from real ads (20% off, 30% off) and a 15% tip on three restaurant bills.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on percent meaning and finding a percent of a quantity.

weeks.topic: Finding the whole and percent problems
objectives: Find the whole given a part and percent
Find what percent one quantity is of another

days.title: Finding the whole
days.work: Solve problems like '12 is 30% of what number?' with tape diagrams and tables (10 problems).

days.title: What percent?
days.work: Find what percent one quantity is of another using nutrition labels (e.g., grams of sugar out of total carbohydrates).

days.title: Battery and progress bars
days.work: Use a device battery percentage and download bars to solve find-the-part, find-the-percent and find-the-whole problems.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Complete a mixed review of unit rates, conversions, speed and percents.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the Unit 3 end-of-unit assessment and correct missed problems.

objectives: Interpret division as 'how many groups' or 'how much in each group'

days.title: Size of divisor and quotient
days.work: Predict and then compute what happens to quotients like 12 / 6, 12 / 1, 12 / 1/2, and write a rule about divisors less than 1.

days.title: Two meanings
days.work: Write two different story problems for 6 / 2 (how many groups vs. how much per group) and draw a diagram for each.

days.title: How many groups?
days.work: Use measuring cups to find how many 1/4 cups fit in 3 cups and how many 3/4 cups fit in 3 cups; record as division equations.

days.title: Using diagrams
days.work: Draw tape diagrams to solve 8 'how many groups' fraction problems, including answers that are not whole numbers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: match equations, diagrams and stories for fraction division.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on interpreting division and fraction diagrams.

objectives: Divide fractions using diagrams and the reciprocal
Explain why multiplying by the reciprocal works

days.title: How much in each group?
days.work: Solve problems like '3/4 of a pound fills 1/2 a bag; how much fills a whole bag?' with tape diagrams (6 problems).

days.title: Dividing by unit fractions
days.work: Notice that dividing by 1/3 is the same as multiplying by 3, and test the pattern with 10 examples.

days.title: Algorithm for fraction division
days.work: Use the reciprocal method to compute 15 quotients including mixed numbers, and check each with multiplication.

days.title: Explain it
days.work: Write a short explanation, with a diagram, of why 2/3 / 1/6 = 4, and critique a sample student's incorrect solution.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on computing fraction quotients and explaining the algorithm.

weeks.assessment: Fraction division computation quiz with one written explanation.

objectives: Solve multi-step fraction division word problems
Use division to find lengths and areas

days.title: Fractional lengths
days.work: Measure a ribbon and find how many 3/8-yard pieces can be cut from 4 1/2 yards; solve 6 similar length problems.

days.title: Rectangles with fractional sides
days.work: Find a missing side when area and one side are fractions (e.g., area 2 1/2 sq ft, width 3/4 ft).

days.title: Recipes
days.work: Scale a recipe calling for 2/3 cup sugar to fit a 1/2-cup measuring scoop and solve 5 recipe-division problems.

days.title: Write your own
days.work: Write and solve three fraction-division story problems and trade with a family member to solve.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on fraction word problems.

objectives: Find volume of prisms with fractional edges
Show V = lwh by packing unit cubes of fractional size

days.title: Packing cubes
days.work: Pack a small box with 1/2-inch cubes, count them, and show that the count x 1/8 cubic inch equals l x w x h.

days.title: Volume formulas
days.work: Compute volumes of 10 prisms with fractional edges using V = lwh and V = Bh.

days.title: Missing dimensions
days.work: Use fraction division to find a missing edge when volume and two edges are known (6 problems).

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Mixed review of fraction division and volume, including one aquarium or garden-bed design problem.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Take the Unit 4 assessment and reflect on the meaning of division.

objectives: Multiply decimals and explain decimal placement

days.title: Decimals in money
days.work: Add and subtract prices from a shopping list, lining up place values, and find change from $50.

days.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
days.work: Solve 20 decimal sums and differences with up to thousandths, including regrouping across zeros.

days.title: Multiplying decimals
days.work: Use area diagrams and fractions (0.3 x 0.4 = 3/10 x 4/10) to explain decimal placement, then compute 12 products.

days.title: Decimal applications
days.work: Calculate total cost of buying fabric at $4.75 per yard for 2.5 yards and 5 similar problems.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on decimal addition, subtraction and multiplication.

objectives: Divide multi-digit whole numbers with the standard algorithm

days.title: Partial quotients
days.work: Divide 3- and 4-digit numbers by 2-digit divisors using partial quotients, then compare to the standard algorithm.

days.title: Long division
days.work: Complete 12 long-division problems with the standard algorithm, checking each by multiplication.

days.title: Dividing decimals
days.work: Divide decimals by whole numbers and by decimals by multiplying both numbers by powers of 10 (12 problems).

days.title: Decimal word problems
days.work: Solve problems such as splitting a $47.85 bill among 3 people and finding miles per gallon.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Semester 1 cumulative review quiz covering area, ratios, percents, fraction division and decimals.

weeks.topic: Factors, multiples and the distributive property
objectives: Factor sums with the distributive property

days.title: Greatest common factor
days.work: Find the largest square tile that exactly covers a 24 x 36 rectangle, then find GCF for 10 pairs of numbers.

days.title: Least common multiple
days.work: Solve 'hot dogs come in 10s, buns in 8s' problems and find LCM for 10 pairs.

days.title: GCF or LCM?
days.work: Sort 8 word problems as GCF or LCM situations and solve each.

days.title: Distributive property
days.work: Rewrite sums like 36 + 8 as 4(9 + 2) using the GCF and use area models to show why it works.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Take the Unit 5 assessment on decimals, long division, GCF/LCM.

objectives: Write expressions with variables from words

days.title: Letters for numbers
days.work: Write expressions for situations such as 'x more than 5' and 'a number divided by 3'; translate 15 phrases into expressions.

days.title: Parts of expressions
days.work: Label terms, coefficients and constants in 10 expressions and describe 2(x + 5) as 'a product of two factors'.

days.title: Expression match
days.work: Play a card-matching game linking verbal descriptions, expressions and tape diagrams.

days.title: Evaluating expressions
days.work: Evaluate 12 expressions for given variable values, e.g., 3x + 4 when x = 2.5.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on writing, reading and evaluating expressions.

objectives: Understand a solution makes an equation true
Solve x + p = q and px = q
materials: balance scale or hanger diagram printouts

days.title: True or false?
days.work: Test whether given values make 10 equations true using substitution.

days.title: Hanger diagrams
days.work: Use hanger diagrams (or a homemade coat-hanger balance with paper clips) to model and solve equations like x + 3 = 7 and 3x = 12.

days.title: Solving addition equations
days.work: Solve 12 equations of the form x + p = q with fractions and decimals, checking by substitution.

days.title: Solving multiplication equations
days.work: Solve 12 equations of the form px = q, including 2/3 x = 10, and write stories for two of them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on solving one-step equations and writing equations for word problems.

objectives: Use properties to write equivalent expressions

days.title: Same value, different form
days.work: Substitute several values into pairs like 3(x + 2) and 3x + 6 to test equivalence, recording results in a table.

days.title: Distributive property with variables
days.work: Use area diagrams to expand 4(x + 3) and factor 6x + 18 (12 problems).

days.title: Combining like terms
days.work: Use paper algebra tiles to simplify expressions like 2x + 5 + 3x + 1 and explain why x + x is 2x.

days.title: Prove or disprove
days.work: Decide whether 8 pairs of expressions are equivalent and justify with properties or a counterexample.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on generating and identifying equivalent expressions.

objectives: Use order of operations including exponents

days.title: Paper-folding powers
days.work: Fold a sheet of paper in half repeatedly, record layers as 2^1, 2^2 ... and predict layers after 10 folds.

days.title: Evaluating powers
days.work: Evaluate 15 expressions such as 3^4, (1/2)^3 and 0.2^2 and compare 2^5 with 5^2.

days.title: Order of operations
days.work: Evaluate 15 expressions like 2 + 3 x 4^2 and (2 + 3)^2 and find the errors in three worked examples.

days.title: Formulas
days.work: Evaluate V = s^3, SA = 6s^2 and A = 1/2 bh for given values, and choose a formula to solve a packaging problem.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on exponents, order of operations and formulas.

weeks.assessment: Exponent and order of operations quiz.

objectives: Represent a relationship with a table, graph and equation

days.title: Two changing quantities
days.work: For situations like 'earning $9 per hour', name the independent and dependent variables and write an equation d = 9h.

days.title: Tables to graphs
days.work: Make tables and first-quadrant graphs for three equations (y = 4x, y = x + 3, y = 2.5x) and compare their shapes.

days.title: Real data
days.work: Fill a cup with water a few tablespoons at a time and weigh it, then make a table, graph and equation for the relationship.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Mixed review of expressions, equations, exponents and variable relationships.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Take the Unit 6 end-of-unit assessment and correct errors.

objectives: Locate rational numbers and opposites on the number line

days.title: Temperature and elevation
days.work: Record temperatures in different places (e.g., Death Valley highs, Lake Tahoe winter lows) and elevations above and below sea level, and explain the meaning of 0.

days.title: Opposites
days.work: Mark 12 numbers and their opposites on a number line, including -2.5 and 3/4, and explain why -(-4) = 4.

days.title: Money and signed numbers
days.work: Represent deposits, withdrawals and debt with positive and negative numbers in 8 situations.

days.title: Rational numbers on the line
days.work: Place fractions and decimals between -3 and 3 on a carefully scaled number line.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on signed numbers in context and number-line placement.

objectives: Interpret absolute value as distance from zero

days.title: Comparing signed numbers
days.work: Write inequality statements comparing pairs like -7 and -3, and explain them as positions on a number line.

days.title: Ordering
days.work: Order sets of rational numbers from least to greatest using a card sort, including fractions and decimals.

days.title: Absolute value
days.work: Find |x| for 12 numbers and interpret absolute value as distance, e.g., a debt of $30 means balance -30.

days.title: Comparing statements
days.work: Distinguish statements about order and about absolute value (e.g., -24 < -14 but |-24| > |-14|) in 8 contexts.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on ordering and absolute value.

objectives: Graph solutions on a number line

days.title: Writing inequalities
days.work: Write inequalities for constraints like 'you must be at least 48 inches to ride' and 'fewer than 30 students' (10 situations).

days.title: Graphing solutions
days.work: Graph x > c, x < c, x >= c and x <= c on number lines and test values with substitution.

days.title: Infinitely many solutions
days.work: Explain why x > 3 has infinitely many solutions and identify whether given values are solutions.

days.title: Inequalities in context
days.work: Solve real problems like saving at least $120 and decide which values make sense in context (whole people, decimals of money).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on writing, graphing and interpreting inequalities.

objectives: Plot points in all four quadrants
Find distances between points with a common coordinate

days.title: Four quadrants
days.work: Plot 20 points including negative and fractional coordinates and name each point's quadrant.

days.title: Reflections
days.work: Reflect points over each axis and describe how the signs of the coordinates change.

days.title: Distances
days.work: Find distances between points like (-3, 4) and (5, 4) using absolute value, in 10 problems.

days.title: Coordinate map
days.work: Draw a neighborhood map on a coordinate grid with home at the origin and solve walking-distance problems along the streets.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on plotting, reflecting and distance.

weeks.assessment: Coordinate plane quiz and map project.

objectives: Find side lengths, perimeter and area using coordinates

days.title: Drawing polygons
days.work: Plot and connect vertices to draw rectangles, triangles and trapezoids in all four quadrants.

days.title: Side lengths
days.work: Use coordinates to find horizontal and vertical side lengths and perimeters of 8 polygons.

days.title: Area on the grid
days.work: Find areas of coordinate polygons by decomposing or enclosing in rectangles.

days.title: Design challenge
days.work: Design a garden plot with 4-6 vertices on Desmos having area exactly 48 square units and list its coordinates.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the Unit 7 end-of-unit assessment on rational numbers, inequalities and the coordinate plane.

days.title: Statistical questions
days.work: Sort 12 questions as statistical or not (e.g., 'How old am I?' vs 'How old are students at my co-op?') and write 3 of your own.

days.title: Collect data
days.work: Survey 20 or more people (family, friends, co-op) with your statistical question and record results in a frequency table.

days.title: Dot plots
days.work: Make a dot plot of your survey data and of a provided data set on daily screen time.

days.title: Describing distributions
days.work: Describe the center, spread and shape (symmetric, skewed, clusters, gaps) of three dot plots in writing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on statistical questions and dot plots.

days.title: Reaction time data
days.work: Measure reaction time 25 times with the ruler-drop test and record the catch distance in centimeters.

days.title: Making histograms
days.work: Group your reaction data into equal bins and draw a histogram with labeled axes.

days.title: Dot plot or histogram?
days.work: Compare a dot plot and histogram of the same data and write when each display is more useful.

days.title: Interpreting histograms
days.work: Answer questions about histograms of California city temperatures and dog weights, describing shape and spread.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on building and reading histograms.

objectives: Understand mean as fair share and balance point

days.title: Fair share
days.work: Use stacks of snap cubes to level out unequal towers and connect the result to adding and dividing.

days.title: Balance point
days.work: Show on a dot plot that the mean is the point where distances above and below balance, using 4 small data sets.

days.title: Mean absolute deviation
days.work: Compute the MAD for two basketball players' points per game and decide who is more consistent.

days.title: Comparing groups
days.work: Compare two data sets (e.g., plant heights with and without fertilizer) using mean and MAD.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on mean and MAD.

objectives: Make box plots and interpret IQR

days.title: Median
days.work: Line up 11 index cards of data to find the median and see why it resists outliers compared with the mean.

days.title: Five-number summary
days.work: Find minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum for 6 data sets and compute range and IQR.

days.title: Box plots
days.work: Draw box plots for your reaction-time data and a family height data set.

days.title: Comparing box plots
days.work: Compare two box plots (e.g., Los Angeles vs San Francisco monthly temperatures) and write 3 conclusions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on median, IQR and box plots.

objectives: Choose appropriate measures of center and spread

days.title: Mean or median?
days.work: Decide for 6 data sets whether mean/MAD or median/IQR better describes them, based on shape and outliers.

days.title: Plan an investigation
days.work: Write a statistical question, plan how to collect at least 30 data points, and begin collecting.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Display your data with two plot types and calculate center and spread measures.

days.title: Present
days.work: Create a poster or slides answering your question with data, and present it to your family.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Take the Unit 8 end-of-unit assessment on data and distributions.

objectives: Apply ratios, percents and decimals to a real plan

days.title: Choose a destination
days.work: Pick a California destination, find the distance, and use a car's miles-per-gallon rate to calculate fuel needed.

days.title: Budget
days.work: Build a budget with lodging, food and tickets, compute totals with decimals and add 8% sales tax.

days.title: Time and speed
days.work: Use average speed to plan driving time and a schedule of stops.

days.title: Packing volume
days.work: Determine whether your luggage (measure boxes or bags) fits a car trunk of given volume, using fractional dimensions.

days.title: Present the plan
days.work: Present your trip plan with all calculations and answer family questions about your choices.

days.title: Review: ratios and number
days.work: Complete a review set on ratios, percents, fraction division and decimals; star problems to revisit.

days.title: Review: expressions and geometry
days.work: Complete a review set on equations, expressions, area, surface area and volume.

courses.subject: SCI
courses.title: Science 6 (Integrated)
courses.description: Grade 6 integrated science follows the California Preferred Integrated Model, connecting physical, Earth and life science through energy. Students investigate thermal energy and design an insulated cooler, explain weather and climate through energy transfer in the atmosphere and ocean, examine natural hazards, explore forces that act at a distance and kinetic and potential energy, and study cells, body systems and senses. Every week includes hands-on investigations with household materials and science notebook writing using claim-evidence-reasoning.
courses.framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 CA Science Framework, Preferred Integrated Course Model, Grade 6

standards.MS-PS1-4: Develop a model that predicts and describes changes in particle motion, temperature and state of a pure substance when thermal energy is added or removed.
standards.MS-PS2-3: Ask questions about data to determine the factors that affect the strength of electric and magnetic forces.
standards.MS-PS2-4: Construct and present arguments using evidence that gravitational interactions are attractive and depend on the masses of interacting objects.
standards.MS-PS2-5: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that fields exist between objects exerting forces on each other even though the objects are not in contact.
standards.MS-PS3-1: Construct and interpret graphical displays of data to describe the relationships of kinetic energy to the mass and speed of an object.
standards.MS-PS3-2: Develop a model to describe that when the arrangement of objects interacting at a distance changes, different amounts of potential energy are stored in the system.
standards.MS-PS3-3: Apply scientific principles to design, construct and test a device that either minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
standards.MS-PS3-4: Plan an investigation to determine the relationships among the energy transferred, the type of matter, the mass, and the change in average kinetic energy of particles (temperature).
standards.MS-PS3-5: Construct, use and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
standards.MS-ESS2-4: Develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth's systems driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.
standards.MS-ESS2-5: Collect data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses result in changes in weather conditions.
standards.MS-ESS2-6: Develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and rotation of the Earth cause patterns of atmospheric and oceanic circulation that determine regional climates.
standards.MS-ESS3-2: Analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effects.
standards.MS-ESS3-5: Ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century.
standards.MS-LS1-1: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells, either one cell or many different numbers and types of cells.
standards.MS-LS1-2: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways the parts of cells contribute to the function.
standards.MS-LS1-3: Use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells.
standards.MS-LS1-8: Gather and synthesize information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli by sending messages to the brain for immediate behavior or storage as memories.
standards.MS-ETS1-1: Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution.
standards.MS-ETS1-2: Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.
standards.MS-ETS1-3: Analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among several design solutions to identify the best characteristics of each.
standards.MS-ETS1-4: Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool or process.
