units.title: Thinking Like Scientists and Engineers
units.big_idea: Scientists ask questions and investigate; engineers define problems with criteria and constraints and test solutions.

units.title: Thermal Energy and Matter
units.big_idea: Temperature measures particle motion; thermal energy moves from warmer to cooler matter and can be controlled by design.

units.title: Weather and the Water Cycle
units.big_idea: The sun's energy and gravity drive the water cycle, and moving air masses produce changing weather.

units.title: Climate and Global Change
units.big_idea: Unequal heating and Earth's rotation set up global circulation patterns that create climates; human activities are warming the planet.

units.title: Natural Hazards
units.big_idea: Data on past hazards help forecast future events and design ways to reduce harm.

units.title: Forces, Fields and Energy
units.big_idea: Objects can push and pull without touching through fields, and energy is stored and transferred as objects move and interact.

units.title: Cells: The Building Blocks of Life
units.big_idea: All living things are made of cells, and the parts of a cell work together to keep it alive.

units.title: Body Systems and the Senses
units.big_idea: The body is a system of interacting subsystems; sensory receptors send messages the brain uses to act and remember.

units.title: Engineering Capstone: Solar Oven
units.big_idea: Engineers use science ideas and iterative testing to optimize a design.

weeks.topic: Scientific investigations and the science notebook
objectives: Identify variables and plan a fair test

days.title: Notebook setup
days.work: Set up a science notebook with table of contents, safety rules and a page explaining what scientists and engineers do differently.

days.title: Testable questions
days.work: Turn 10 'wonder' questions into testable questions and identify independent and dependent variables in each.

days.title: Paper towel investigation
days.work: Design and run a fair test of which paper towel absorbs the most water, keeping water amount and soaking time constant.

days.title: Data and graphs
days.work: Organize results in a data table, calculate averages of three trials and draw a bar graph.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion for the paper towel test and quiz on variables.

objectives: Evaluate design solutions with a decision matrix

days.title: Defining problems
days.work: Analyze three everyday products (e.g., a lunch box) and list their criteria and constraints.

days.title: Index card bridge
days.work: Design and build a bridge from 10 index cards and 30 cm of tape that spans 20 cm and holds the most pennies.

days.title: Test and redesign
days.work: Test the bridge, record the penny count, then redesign and retest once.

days.title: Decision matrix
days.work: Score three bridge designs (yours and two sketches) in a weighted decision matrix and choose the best.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short engineering report: problem, criteria, constraints, designs tested and results.

objectives: Relate temperature to average kinetic energy
materials: cups of hot and cold water

days.title: Food coloring in hot and cold water
days.work: Add a drop of food coloring to cups of hot and cold water at the same time, time how long each takes to mix, and record observations.

days.title: Particle model
days.work: Draw particle models of the two cups and explain the difference using particle motion.

days.title: Simulation
days.work: Use the PhET States of Matter simulation to heat and cool a substance and record how particle speed changes with temperature.

days.title: How thermometers work
days.work: Build a simple thermometer from a bottle, colored water and a straw, and test it in warm and cool water baths.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER explaining why food coloring spreads faster in hot water; quiz on temperature vs. thermal energy.

objectives: Model what happens to particles during melting, freezing, evaporating and condensing

days.title: Heating curve lab
days.work: With adult help, heat ice in a pot, recording temperature every 30 seconds until the water boils.

days.title: Graph the data
days.work: Graph temperature vs. time and identify the flat sections where the state changes.

days.title: Why the plateau?
days.work: Use particle models to explain why temperature stays constant while ice melts and water boils.

days.title: Condensation and freezing
days.work: Observe condensation on a cold glass and freeze water in a cup; model particles during cooling.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw and label a complete particle model of all state changes and take a quiz on heating curves.

objectives: Distinguish the three methods of thermal energy transfer
Explain transfer from hot to cold

days.title: Spoon conduction race
days.work: Put a dab of butter on metal, wooden and plastic spoons standing in hot water and record which melts first.

days.title: Convection currents
days.work: Drop cold blue-dyed water into warm water in a clear container and sketch the convection current.

days.title: Radiation
days.work: Place thermometers under black and white paper in sunlight or under a lamp and record temperatures every 2 minutes for 20 minutes.

days.title: Reaching equilibrium
days.work: Mix equal amounts of hot and cold water and measure the final temperature; explain energy flow from hot to cold.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label conduction, convection and radiation in a diagram of a campfire and a kitchen; quiz on transfer methods.

objectives: Plan an investigation of how mass and type of matter affect temperature change

days.title: Plan the investigation
days.work: Plan an investigation comparing temperature change of 100 g vs. 200 g of water given equal heating time; identify variables.

days.title: Mass investigation
days.work: Run the mass investigation under a lamp, recording temperature every 2 minutes.

days.title: Sand vs. water
days.work: Heat equal masses of sand and water for 15 minutes and compare temperature changes; connect to beaches and coastal climates.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Graph both investigations and write how mass and type of matter affect temperature change.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER answering why the beach sand is hotter than the ocean on a sunny afternoon.

weeks.assessment: Lab report with graphs and CER.

objectives: Design, build and test a device that minimizes thermal energy transfer
Analyze test data to improve a design

days.title: Define the problem
days.work: Define criteria (an ice cube loses the least mass in 60 minutes) and constraints (materials list, size) for an ice cube keeper.

days.title: Design and build
days.work: Sketch two designs, choose one using science ideas about conduction, convection and radiation, and build it.

days.title: Test
days.work: Weigh an ice cube, keep it in your device for 60 minutes alongside a control cup, then weigh the remaining ice.

days.title: Redesign
days.work: Analyze which features worked, modify the design and retest.

days.title: Present and check
days.work: Present your data and final design, explaining how it reduces each type of heat transfer; take the unit test.

weeks.assessment: Design challenge rubric and Unit 2 test.

objectives: Model how sun and gravity drive water through Earth's systems

days.title: Water cycle in a bowl
days.work: Build a mini water cycle (bowl with warm salty water, cup in middle, plastic wrap and ice on top) and observe after an hour.

days.title: Transpiration
days.work: Tie a plastic bag around a leafy branch and record water collected after 24 hours; explain transpiration.

days.title: Energy in the cycle
days.work: Draw a water cycle model labeling where energy from the sun and the force of gravity drive each process.

days.title: California's water
days.work: Trace how Sierra Nevada snowmelt reaches California homes using a map; discuss droughts and the snowpack.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain why the water in the bowl's center cup was not salty (CER) and quiz on water cycle processes.

objectives: Investigate air pressure and its relationship to temperature

days.title: Layers of air
days.work: Create a scaled drawing of atmospheric layers and note where weather happens.

days.title: Air has pressure
days.work: Demonstrate air pressure with the index-card-on-a-cup-of-water trick and the crushed bottle (warm air cooling inside a capped bottle).

days.title: Build a barometer
days.work: Build a jar-and-balloon barometer with a straw pointer and begin recording daily readings.

days.title: Warm air rises
days.work: Hold a paper spiral above a warm lamp or radiator and explain the motion using density.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on atmosphere and air pressure; compare your barometer readings with the weather.

days.title: Cloud in a jar
days.work: With adult help, make a cloud in a jar using warm water, ice and a little smoke, and explain the role of cooling and particles.

days.title: Dew point
days.work: Add ice slowly to water in a metal can, stirring, and record the temperature when dew forms.

days.title: Cloud types
days.work: Observe and photograph clouds daily, identify them with a cloud chart and relate them to weather that followed.

days.title: Precipitation
days.work: Read about how droplets grow into rain, snow, sleet and hail, and make a diagram of each.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on humidity, clouds and precipitation types.

days.title: Air mass types
days.work: Learn the four air mass types (maritime/continental, tropical/polar) and identify which ones affect California.

days.title: Front model
days.work: Model a front with warm red water and cold blue water separated by a divider; remove it and sketch what happens.

days.title: Reading weather maps
days.work: Interpret front symbols, highs and lows on three daily NOAA weather maps.

days.title: Weather data
days.work: Collect a week of local temperature, pressure, wind and humidity data and connect changes to fronts on maps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER explaining a weather change you observed using air mass and front data.

days.title: Make a forecast
days.work: Use your barometer, cloud and wind observations to forecast tomorrow's weather and check the next day.

days.title: Thunderstorms
days.work: Diagram the stages of a thunderstorm and explain the roles of rising warm air and condensation.

days.title: Atmospheric rivers
days.work: Read about atmospheric rivers that bring California winter storms and trace one on a satellite image.

days.title: Weather report
days.work: Write and record a 2-minute TV-style weather report for your town using real data.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on water cycle, air pressure, air masses and forecasting.

objectives: Explain why the equator receives more energy than the poles
Model global wind patterns and the Coriolis effect

days.title: Flashlight angles
days.work: Shine a flashlight on graph paper straight down and at an angle; count squares lit to model why the equator is warmer.

days.title: Convection cells
days.work: Draw global convection cells (Hadley, Ferrel, polar) and explain how they form from uneven heating.

days.title: Coriolis effect
days.work: Draw a straight line on a spinning paper plate to model the Coriolis effect and explain curved winds.

days.title: Global wind map
days.work: Label trade winds, westerlies and polar easterlies on a world map and explain which affects California.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on uneven heating and global winds.

objectives: Explain how ocean currents distribute energy
Explain how geography shapes regional climates

days.title: Wind-driven currents
days.work: Blow across water in a baking dish with pepper flakes to model wind-driven currents and sketch the pattern.

days.title: California Current
days.work: Compare San Francisco and Washington, D.C. temperatures at similar latitudes and explain the role of the cold California Current.

days.title: Rain shadow
days.work: Model a rain shadow with a cardboard mountain and spray bottle; compare rainfall on both sides of the Sierra Nevada using data.

days.title: Climographs
days.work: Make climographs for San Diego, Sacramento and Death Valley and explain their differences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER on why two places at the same latitude have different climates.

objectives: Ask questions about factors causing warming

days.title: Greenhouse model
days.work: Place thermometers in a covered and an uncovered jar under a lamp and record temperatures every 2 minutes for 20 minutes.

days.title: Reading the graphs
days.work: Analyze NASA global temperature and atmospheric CO2 graphs and describe trends since 1900.

days.title: Asking questions
days.work: Write 8 questions to clarify evidence about causes of warming (solar output, volcanoes, CO2) and research answers on NASA Climate Kids.

days.title: California impacts
days.work: Read about changes to California's snowpack and wildfire seasons and discuss solutions families and communities use.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Unit 4 test on climate, circulation and global temperature change.

weeks.assessment: Greenhouse lab write-up and Unit 4 test.

objectives: Analyze patterns in natural hazard data

days.title: Earthquake data
days.work: Use the USGS 'Latest Earthquakes' map to record 20 California earthquakes from the past month and plot them on a map.

days.title: Patterns along faults
days.work: Compare your map with a map of the San Andreas fault system and describe the pattern.

days.title: Landslide tray
days.work: Build a sand slope in a tray and add water gradually to observe when a landslide happens; relate to wildfire burn scars and storms.

days.title: Volcano monitoring
days.work: Read how scientists monitor Mount Shasta and Lassen with seismometers and gas sensors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on hazard patterns and forecasting.

objectives: Design solutions to reduce hazard damage
Evaluate technologies such as early warning systems

days.title: Shake table
days.work: Build a simple shake table from cardboard and rubber bands and test a sugar-cube tower.

days.title: Earthquake-resistant design
days.work: Redesign the tower with cross-bracing or base isolation and test again, recording results.

days.title: Early warning
days.work: Learn how California's MyShake/ShakeAlert early warning system uses data and write how seconds of warning help.

days.title: Family hazard plan
days.work: Create a family emergency plan and kit list for an earthquake or wildfire.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present your shake-table results and family plan; take the Unit 5 test.

weeks.assessment: Shake-table design report and Unit 5 test.

days.title: Magnet exploration
days.work: Test which household objects are attracted to a magnet and how poles interact; record results.

days.title: Distance and strength
days.work: Measure how many paper clips a magnet holds at different distances through layers of paper; graph the data.

days.title: Mapping fields
days.work: Map the magnetic field around a bar magnet using a compass or iron filings under paper and draw field lines.

days.title: Earth's field
days.work: Make a compass by magnetizing a needle and floating it on a cork; explain Earth's magnetic field.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER on how distance affects magnetic force using your graph.

days.title: Static electricity
days.work: Rub a balloon on hair and test its pull on tissue bits and a stream of tap water at different distances.

days.title: Charges
days.work: Model positive and negative charges and explain attraction and repulsion between two charged balloons.

days.title: Build an electromagnet
days.work: With adult supervision, wrap wire around a nail, connect to a battery and count paper clips picked up.

days.title: Variables
days.work: Test how the number of coils (10, 20, 30) affects electromagnet strength and graph results.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on electric and magnetic forces and write questions you would investigate next.

objectives: Argue that gravity is attractive and depends on mass

days.title: Falling objects
days.work: Drop objects of different masses (a book and a crumpled paper) and test whether they fall at the same rate.

days.title: Mass vs. weight
days.work: Calculate your weight on the Moon, Mars and Jupiter using gravity ratios and explain why mass stays the same.

days.title: Orbits simulation
days.work: Use PhET Gravity and Orbits to change the Sun's and Earth's masses and record effects on the orbit.

days.title: Ball on a string
days.work: Swing a ball on a string to model an orbit and explain what happens when the string (gravity) is removed.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an argument with evidence that gravitational force depends on mass and distance.

objectives: Graph the relationship of kinetic energy to mass and speed

days.title: Energy of motion
days.work: Roll a ball down a ramp into a paper cup and measure how far the cup slides as evidence of kinetic energy.

days.title: Mass investigation
days.work: Use balls of different mass from the same ramp height and record cup distance in three trials each.

days.title: Speed investigation
days.work: Release the same ball from three ramp heights (different speeds) and record cup distance.

days.title: Graph it
days.work: Graph cup distance vs. mass and vs. speed and describe which relationship is steeper.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER explaining why a speeding car is much more dangerous than a slow one (speed squared relationship).

objectives: Model how changing arrangement changes stored potential energy

days.title: Height and energy
days.work: Drop a ball into flour or sand from 3 heights and measure crater depth as evidence of stored energy.

days.title: Elastic energy
days.work: Launch rubber bands from a ruler at different stretch lengths and measure distance traveled.

days.title: Magnetic potential energy
days.work: Hold two magnets at different separations and explain where energy is stored in the system.

days.title: Energy Skate Park
days.work: Use PhET Energy Skate Park to track potential and kinetic energy bar graphs as the skater moves.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw energy models for a roller coaster at four points and take a quiz on potential energy.

objectives: Argue that changing kinetic energy means energy is transferred
materials: foam pipe insulation cut in half

days.title: Where does energy go?
days.work: Rub hands together and bounce a ball until it stops; explain the energy transfers to thermal energy and sound.

days.title: Roller coaster design
days.work: Design a marble roller coaster from foam pipe insulation with a loop, defining criteria and constraints.

days.title: Build and test
days.work: Build and test the coaster, adjusting starting height so the marble completes the loop.

days.title: Energy argument
days.work: Write an argument explaining energy transfers at each part of your coaster, including friction.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Unit 6 test on forces, fields and energy.

weeks.topic: Discovering cells and using a microscope
objectives: Describe the history of cell discovery
Use a microscope or magnifier to observe cells

days.title: Cell theory history
days.work: Read about Hooke, Leeuwenhoek and the cell theory and make a timeline of discoveries.

days.title: Microscope skills
days.work: Learn microscope parts and practice focusing on a newspaper letter 'e', noting how the image flips.

days.title: Cork cells
days.work: Observe a thin slice of cork as Hooke did and sketch what you see with magnification noted.

days.title: Onion cells
days.work: Prepare an onion skin wet mount with iodine or food coloring and draw the cells.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on cell theory and microscope parts and use.

weeks.topic: Living things are made of cells
objectives: Provide evidence that living things are unicellular or multicellular

days.title: Is it alive?
days.work: Sort 15 items as living, once living or nonliving using characteristics of life.

days.title: Yeast are alive
days.work: Mix yeast, sugar and warm water in a bottle with a balloon on top, and record balloon size every 10 minutes.

days.title: Pond water
days.work: Observe pond water or a hay infusion under the microscope and sketch single-celled organisms.

days.title: Cheek cells
days.work: Gently swab your inner cheek, stain with food coloring and observe human cells; compare with onion cells.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER that yeast is a living, single-celled organism using balloon data.

days.title: Organelles
days.work: Learn the function of each major organelle and complete a labeled diagram of an animal cell.

days.title: Plant vs. animal
days.work: Compare plant and animal cells in a Venn diagram and relate differences to how plants make food.

days.title: Edible cell model
days.work: Build a cell model in a bag of gelatin using food items for organelles, with a key explaining each choice.

days.title: Cell analogy
days.work: Write a 'cell is like a city' analogy explaining the role of at least 7 organelles.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on organelle functions.

weeks.topic: The cell membrane and getting materials
objectives: Model how the membrane controls what enters and leaves

days.title: Naked egg
days.work: Soak a raw egg in vinegar to dissolve the shell, measuring circumference before and after.

days.title: Egg osmosis
days.work: Move the shell-less egg into corn syrup and later water, measuring and explaining size changes with osmosis.

days.title: Potato osmosis
days.work: Soak potato slices in plain and salty water and compare their mass and stiffness after an hour.

days.title: Diffusion
days.work: Place a scented extract in a balloon and detect diffusion through the membrane; model particle movement.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a lab report explaining how the egg membrane acts like a cell membrane.

objectives: Explain cell division for growth and repair

days.title: Specialized cells
days.work: Compare nerve, muscle, red blood and skin cells and explain how shape fits function.

days.title: Levels of organization
days.work: Create a nested diagram from cell to tissue to organ to organ system to organism with examples.

days.title: Cell division
days.work: Make a flip book showing a cell dividing and explain why cells divide for growth and repair.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Review cells with a concept map linking all unit vocabulary.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on cells and their parts.

objectives: Explain how bones and muscles work together
materials: chicken wing (cooked or raw with gloves)

days.title: Bones
days.work: Identify 15 major bones on a diagram and feel the bones of your hand and arm.

days.title: Joints
days.work: Test range of motion of hinge, ball-and-socket and pivot joints on your body and record findings.

days.title: Muscle pairs
days.work: Build a cardboard arm model with string 'muscles' to show biceps and triceps working in pairs.

days.title: Chicken wing
days.work: With gloves, examine a chicken wing to find muscles, tendons and bone and sketch them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on bones, joints and muscle pairs.

objectives: Explain how the heart and lungs work together
Measure heart rate and breathing rate

days.title: Heart rate investigation
days.work: Measure resting heart rate and heart rate after 1 minute of jumping jacks, three trials each, and graph.

days.title: Path of blood
days.work: Trace the path of blood through the heart, lungs and body on a diagram.

days.title: Lung model
days.work: Build a bottle-and-balloon lung model and explain how the diaphragm moves air.

days.title: Systems interact
days.work: Explain in writing how the circulatory and respiratory systems interact during exercise using your heart rate data.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER arguing that the body is a system of interacting subsystems using exercise data.

objectives: Explain how digestion connects to circulation and cells

days.title: Digestion in a bag
days.work: Model chemical and mechanical digestion by mashing crackers with water and vinegar in a bag, then squeezing through a 'small intestine' stocking.

days.title: Length of the gut
days.work: Measure out 9 meters of string to represent the digestive tract and label each organ's section.

days.title: Saliva enzyme
days.work: Chew a plain cracker for 1 minute and note the change in taste; explain how enzymes break starch into sugar.

days.title: System connections
days.work: Map how nutrients travel from the small intestine through blood to cells and how kidneys remove waste.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on the digestive and excretory systems.

objectives: Explain how sensory receptors send messages to the brain

days.title: Neurons and messages
days.work: Diagram a neuron and the pathway from receptor to spinal cord to brain to muscle.

days.title: Reaction time
days.work: Run the ruler-drop reaction test 10 times with each hand and compare averages.

days.title: Touch receptors
days.work: Use a two-point test with paper clips on fingertip, palm and forearm to map receptor density.

days.title: Taste and smell
days.work: Blindfolded, taste jelly beans with and without holding your nose and record identification accuracy.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER explaining why smell affects taste, using your data.

objectives: Gather information on how the brain stores memories

days.title: Memory tray
days.work: Study a tray of 20 objects for 1 minute, cover it, and list what you remember; repeat with a memory strategy and compare.

days.title: Optical illusions
days.work: Investigate three optical illusions and explain how the brain interprets signals from the eyes.

days.title: Research
days.work: Read two sources about how memories form and summarize them in a one-page infographic.

days.title: Body systems poster
days.work: Create a poster showing how at least four body systems work together when you catch a ball.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Unit 8 test on body systems and senses.

objectives: Define criteria and constraints for a solar oven
Apply thermal energy ideas to a design

days.title: The problem
days.work: Research how solar ovens are used around the world and define criteria (reach 60 C) and constraints (materials, cost).

days.title: Science ideas
days.work: List how reflection, absorption, insulation and the greenhouse effect could each help the oven.

days.title: Sketch designs
days.work: Sketch three designs and evaluate them with a decision matrix.

days.title: Build prototype
days.work: Build the chosen solar oven from a pizza box and household materials.

days.title: Check-in
days.work: Write a design brief explaining your choices and predict the maximum temperature.

objectives: Modify the design based on data

days.title: First test
days.work: Test the oven in direct sun, recording internal temperature every 5 minutes for 45 minutes.

days.title: Analyze

days.title: Modify
days.work: Make one change (extra reflector, insulation, angle) and record why you chose it.

days.title: Second test
days.work: Retest and try to melt a s'more; compare the two graphs.

days.title: Check-in
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining how the modification affected thermal energy transfer.

objectives: Review major ideas of grade 6 science

days.title: Prepare presentation
days.work: Create a presentation of your solar oven design process with photos, graphs and conclusions.

days.title: Present

days.title: Year review: energy
days.work: Make a concept map showing how energy connects thermal energy, weather, forces and living systems.

days.work: Take a cumulative assessment covering all units.

courses.subject: HSS
courses.title: World History and Geography: Ancient Civilizations
courses.description: Students study the peoples and civilizations of the ancient world from early humans through the fall of Rome: Mesopotamia, Egypt and Kush, ancient Israel, Greece, India, China and Rome. They use maps, timelines, archaeology and primary sources (the Code of Hammurabi, Egyptian hymns, the Hebrew Bible, Pericles' Funeral Oration, Ashoka's edicts, the Analects, Roman law and more) to explain how geography, religion, government, trade and ideas shaped societies whose legacies remain today. Religions are studied academically, as the HSS Framework directs, to understand their history and influence.
courses.framework: California History-Social Science Content Standards (Grade 6); 2016 CA History-Social Science Framework, Chapter 10

standards.6.1: Students describe what is known through archaeological studies of the early physical and cultural development of humankind from the Paleolithic era to the agricultural revolution.
standards.6.1.1: Describe the hunter-gatherer societies, including the development of tools and the use of fire.
standards.6.1.2: Identify the locations of human communities that populated the major regions of the world and describe how humans adapted to a variety of environments.
standards.6.1.3: Discuss the climatic changes and human modifications of the environment that gave rise to the domestication of plants and animals and new sources of clothing and shelter.
standards.6.2: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of Mesopotamia, Egypt and Kush.
standards.6.2.1: Locate and describe the major river systems and the physical settings that supported permanent settlement and early civilizations.
standards.6.2.2: Trace the development of agricultural techniques that permitted economic surplus and the emergence of cities as centers of culture and power.
standards.6.2.3: Understand the relationship between religion and the social and political order in Mesopotamia and Egypt.
standards.6.2.4: Know the significance of Hammurabi's Code.
standards.6.2.5: Discuss the main features of Egyptian art and architecture.
standards.6.2.6: Describe the role of Egyptian trade in the eastern Mediterranean and Nile valley.
standards.6.2.7: Understand the significance of Queen Hatshepsut and Ramses the Great.
standards.6.2.8: Identify the location of the Kush civilization and describe its political, commercial and cultural relations with Egypt.
standards.6.2.9: Trace the evolution of language and its written forms.
standards.6.3: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the Ancient Hebrews.
standards.6.3.1: Describe the origins and significance of Judaism as the first monotheistic religion based on the concept of one God who sets down moral laws for humanity.
standards.6.3.2: Identify the sources of the ethical teachings and central beliefs of Judaism and how they are reflected in the moral and ethical traditions of Western civilization.
standards.6.3.3: Explain the significance of Abraham, Moses, Naomi, Ruth, David and Yohanan ben Zaccai in the development of the Jewish religion.
standards.6.3.4: Discuss the locations of the settlements and movements of Hebrew peoples, including the Exodus, and outline the significance of the Exodus.
standards.6.3.5: Discuss how Judaism survived and developed despite continuing dispersion (the Diaspora), including the destruction of the Second Temple and the academy at Yavneh.
standards.6.4: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of Ancient Greece.
standards.6.4.1: Discuss the connections between geography and the development of city-states in the region of the Aegean Sea, including patterns of trade and commerce.
standards.6.4.2: Trace the transition from tyranny and oligarchy to early democratic forms of government and back to dictatorship, including Pericles' Funeral Oration.
standards.6.4.3: State the key differences between Athenian, or direct, democracy and representative democracy.
standards.6.4.4: Explain the significance of Greek mythology to everyday life and literature, including Homer's Iliad and Odyssey and Aesop's Fables.
standards.6.4.5: Outline the founding, expansion and political organization of the Persian Empire.
standards.6.4.6: Compare and contrast life in Athens and Sparta, with emphasis on their roles in the Persian and Peloponnesian Wars.
standards.6.4.7: Trace the rise of Alexander the Great and the spread of Greek culture eastward and into Egypt.
standards.6.4.8: Describe the enduring contributions of important Greek figures in the arts and sciences (e.g., Hypatia, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Euclid, Thucydides).
standards.6.5: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of India.
standards.6.5.1: Locate and describe the major river system and discuss the physical setting that supported the rise of this civilization.
standards.6.5.2: Discuss the significance of the Aryan (Indo-Aryan) migrations.
standards.6.5.3: Explain the major beliefs and practices of Brahmanism in India and how they evolved into early Hinduism.
standards.6.5.4: Outline the social structure of the caste system.
standards.6.5.5: Know the life and moral teachings of Buddha and how Buddhism spread in India, Ceylon and Central Asia.
standards.6.5.6: Describe the growth of the Maurya empire and the political and moral achievements of the emperor Asoka.
standards.6.5.7: Discuss important aesthetic and intellectual traditions (e.g., Sanskrit literature including the Bhagavad Gita; medicine; metallurgy; mathematics, including Hindu-Arabic numerals and zero).
standards.6.6: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of China.
standards.6.6.1: Locate and describe the origins of Chinese civilization in the Huang-He Valley during the Shang Dynasty.
standards.6.6.2: Explain the geographic features of China that made governance and the spread of ideas and goods difficult and served to isolate the country.
standards.6.6.3: Know about the life of Confucius and the fundamental teachings of Confucianism and Daoism.
standards.6.6.4: Identify the political and cultural problems prevalent in the time of Confucius and how he sought to solve them.
standards.6.6.5: List the policies and achievements of the emperor Shi Huangdi in unifying northern China under the Qin Dynasty.
standards.6.6.6: Detail the political contributions of the Han Dynasty to the development of the imperial bureaucratic state and the expansion of the empire.
standards.6.6.7: Cite the significance of the trans-Eurasian 'silk roads' in the period of the Han Dynasty and Roman Empire and their locations.
standards.6.6.8: Describe the diffusion of Buddhism northward to China during the Han Dynasty.
standards.6.7: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures during the development of Rome.
standards.6.7.1: Identify the location and describe the rise of the Roman Republic, including the importance of figures such as Aeneas, Romulus and Remus, Cincinnatus, Julius Caesar and Cicero.
standards.6.7.2: Describe the government of the Roman Republic and its significance (written constitution, tripartite government, checks and balances, civic duty).
standards.6.7.3: Identify the location of and reasons for the growth of Roman territories and how the empire fostered economic growth through currency and trade routes.
standards.6.7.4: Discuss the influence of Julius Caesar and Augustus in Rome's transition from republic to empire.
standards.6.7.5: Trace the migration of Jews around the Mediterranean region and the effects of their conflict with the Romans, including restrictions on their right to live in Jerusalem.
standards.6.7.6: Note the origins of Christianity in Jewish Messianic prophecies, the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth as described in the New Testament, and the contribution of Paul the Apostle.
standards.6.7.7: Describe the circumstances that led to the spread of Christianity in Europe and other Roman territories.
standards.6.7.8: Discuss the legacies of Roman art and architecture, technology and science, literature, language and law.
standards.CST.1: Analysis skill: Explain how major events are related to one another in time (chronological thinking, timelines, BCE/CE).
standards.CST.3: Analysis skill: Use a variety of maps and documents to identify physical and cultural features and explain historical migration and settlement patterns.
standards.REP.2: Analysis skill: Distinguish relevant from irrelevant information and essential from incidental information in historical narratives.
standards.REP.4: Analysis skill: Assess the credibility of primary and secondary sources and draw sound conclusions from them.
standards.HI.1: Analysis skill: Explain the central issues and problems from the past, placing people and events in a matrix of time and place.

units.title: Early Humankind and the Agricultural Revolution
units.big_idea: Archaeology reveals how early humans adapted to environments and how farming changed the way people lived.

units.title: Mesopotamia: The Fertile Crescent
units.big_idea: Rivers, surplus and writing allowed the first cities, kingdoms and written laws.

units.title: Ancient Egypt and Kush
units.big_idea: The Nile shaped a long-lasting civilization whose religion, rulers, art and trade linked it to Kush and the Mediterranean.

units.title: Ancient Israel and the Origins of Judaism
units.big_idea: The ancient Hebrews developed monotheism and ethical teachings that endured through exile and dispersion.

units.title: Ancient Greece
units.big_idea: Greek city-states experimented with government, fought for survival and produced ideas in art, science and philosophy still used today.

units.title: Ancient India
units.big_idea: From the Indus cities to the Maurya Empire, India developed major religions, a complex social structure and lasting achievements in mathematics and literature.

units.title: Ancient China
units.big_idea: China's geography, philosophies and dynasties created a unified bureaucratic state connected to the world by the Silk Roads.

units.title: Ancient Rome
units.big_idea: Rome grew from a republic to an empire whose law, language, engineering and religions shaped the Western world.

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Explain the link between religion and political order

days.title: Ziggurats

days.title: Unit 2 test

courses.subject: VAPA
courses.title: Visual and Performing Arts 6
courses.description: A year-long arts survey aligned to the 2019 California Arts Standards. Students keep a sketchbook, study the elements and principles of art, create works inspired by the ancient civilizations they study in history, learn one- and two-point perspective, read and compose music, improvise and perform theatre scenes, make a stop-motion animation, choreograph a short dance and curate a final portfolio exhibition.

days.work: Compare black-figure and red-figure vases from the Met's collection and list differences.

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a vase showing a myth or a modern event with a Greek key border.

days.title: Create
days.work: Create the vase in black-figure style with cut paper or on an air-dry clay pot.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Present the story on your vase and evaluate your use of border patterns.

objectives: Interpret mandalas, Buddhist art and Chinese brush painting

days.title: Mandalas
days.work: Study mandala designs and create a radially symmetric mandala using a compass and protractor.

days.title: Buddhist sculpture
days.work: Analyze images of Gandharan and Chinese Buddha sculptures and note how style changed as Buddhism spread.

days.title: Brush strokes
days.work: Practice basic Chinese brush strokes and paint bamboo stalks and leaves.

days.title: Ink landscape
days.work: Paint a vertical scroll landscape with mountains and mist using ink wash values.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Compare your mandala and scroll and write how each reflects its culture's values.

objectives: Analyze how museums preserve ancient art
materials: colored paper squares or dried beans

days.title: Roman mosaics
days.work: Study Pompeii mosaics (e.g., 'Cave Canem') and identify how tesserae create shading.

days.title: Plan a mosaic
days.work: Sketch a mosaic design and plan colors on a grid.

days.title: Build the mosaic
days.work: Glue paper or bean tesserae onto cardboard, leaving even grout lines.

days.title: Preservation
days.work: Watch a museum conservation video and compare how 2D, 3D and digital works are preserved.

days.title: Review & critique
days.work: Display your ancient-art pieces together and write a critique of your strongest work using your criteria.

objectives: Use a horizon line and vanishing point
Draw a room in one-point perspective

days.title: Finding vanishing points
days.work: Trace orthogonal lines on photos of roads and hallways to locate vanishing points.

days.title: Floating boxes
days.work: Draw 8 boxes above, below and on the horizon line using one vanishing point.

days.title: Hallway
days.work: Draw a hallway with doors and windows in one-point perspective.

days.title: Your room
days.work: Draw your bedroom in one-point perspective with furniture.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Self-check orthogonals with a ruler and fix any errors.

objectives: Draw forms with two vanishing points

days.title: Two-point boxes
days.work: Draw boxes using two vanishing points on a long sheet of paper.

days.title: Buildings
days.work: Turn boxes into buildings with doors, windows and roofs.

days.title: Cityscape
days.work: Draw a street corner cityscape in two-point perspective.

days.title: Atmospheric perspective
days.work: Color the cityscape using brighter, sharper colors in front and lighter, cooler colors far away.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Revise one area of your cityscape based on a parent's critique.

objectives: Design a space that meets users' needs

days.title: Interview a user
days.work: Interview a family member about what they would need in a dream reading nook or community space.

days.title: Floor plan
days.work: Draw a floor plan to scale that meets those needs, including accessibility features.

days.title: Perspective view
days.work: Draw a perspective view of your design.

days.title: Model
days.work: Build a small cardboard model of the space.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Present your design and explain how it meets the user's needs.

days.title: Analyze posters
days.work: Analyze three public service posters (e.g., WPA National Park posters) for focal point, color and text.

days.title: Plan a message
days.work: Choose a message (water conservation, reading) and sketch three thumbnail layouts.

days.title: Lettering
days.work: Practice block and decorative lettering for your headline.

days.title: Final poster
days.work: Create the final poster with a clear focal point and limited color palette.

days.title: Review & critique
days.work: Ask two viewers what the message is and revise if they misread it.

objectives: Read and perform rhythms with whole through sixteenth notes

days.title: Beat vs. rhythm
days.work: Tap the steady beat and then the rhythm of three songs and explain the difference.

days.title: Note values
days.work: Complete musictheory.net lessons on note and rest durations and clap 8 written rhythm patterns.

days.title: Time signatures
days.work: Identify 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 in recordings by counting and conducting patterns.

days.title: Bucket drumming
days.work: Play a 4-measure bucket-drum rhythm with sixteenth notes from notation.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a rhythm reading test of 4 patterns with a metronome.

objectives: Read notes on the treble clef
Begin an instrument (recorder, keyboard or ukulele)

days.title: Treble clef
days.work: Learn line and space notes (EGBDF, FACE) and complete a note-naming drill.

days.title: First notes
days.work: Learn to play B, A and G (recorder) or C-D-E (keyboard) and play 'Hot Cross Buns' from notation.

days.title: Bass clef
days.work: Learn bass clef notes and name 20 notes in a timed drill.

days.title: Expanding range
days.work: Add two new notes and play 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' and 'Ode to Joy' (first phrase).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a note-naming quiz and play a short melody for a family member.

objectives: Perform a melody with correct rhythm

days.title: Whole and half steps
days.work: Find whole and half steps on a keyboard diagram and build the C major scale.

days.title: Major vs. minor
days.work: Listen to major and minor versions of the same tune in Chrome Music Lab and describe the mood.

days.title: Practice with criteria
days.work: Practice 'Ode to Joy' using criteria (steady tempo, correct notes, good tone) and mark trouble spots.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Slow-practice the trouble spots with a metronome and gradually increase tempo.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record a performance of the scale and melody and evaluate it with the criteria.

days.title: Dynamics
days.work: Listen to Ravel's 'Bolero' and chart how dynamics grow; learn p, mp, mf, f symbols.

days.title: Tempo
days.work: Learn Italian tempo terms and match them to five recorded excerpts.

days.title: Articulation
days.work: Play a melody legato and staccato and explain how it changes character.

days.title: Expressive performance
days.work: Add dynamics and articulation to your melody and practice following markings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on musical terms and perform your melody with expression.

objectives: Sing with good posture and breath support
materials: lyrics for rounds ('Dona Nobis Pacem', 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat')

days.title: Vocal warm-ups
days.work: Learn breathing and vocal warm-ups and sing a major scale on solfege.

days.title: Rounds
days.work: Sing 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat' as a round with family members.

days.title: Two-part harmony
days.work: Learn 'Dona Nobis Pacem' and sing one part while a recording or family member sings another.

days.title: Rehearsal
days.work: Rehearse a song and an instrumental piece for a mini-concert using performance criteria.

days.title: Mid-year concert
days.work: Perform a mid-year family concert (one song, one instrumental piece) and self-evaluate.

objectives: Identify instruments and features of world music
Perform a rhythm from another culture
materials: recordings of Indian, Chinese, West African and Mexican music

days.title: India
days.work: Listen to a sitar raga and identify the drone and tala rhythm cycle.

days.title: China
days.work: Listen to guzheng music and play a pentatonic melody on black keys of a keyboard or a xylophone app.

days.title: West Africa
days.work: Learn a West African polyrhythm with two household percussion instruments.

days.title: Mexico
days.work: Listen to mariachi music and identify instruments and the son jalisciense rhythm.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a listening quiz identifying four world music traditions by sound.

objectives: Identify AB, ABA and rondo forms
materials: recordings of Mozart 'Twinkle Variations', Beethoven 'Fur Elise'

days.title: AB and ABA
days.work: Listen to songs and label AB and ABA sections using shapes and colors.

days.title: Rondo
days.work: Map the ABACA form of Beethoven's 'Fur Elise'.

days.title: Theme and variations
days.work: Listen to Mozart's 'Twelve Variations on Ah vous dirai-je, Maman' and describe how three variations change the theme.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Choose two contrasting pieces you like and compare their form, purpose and mood in writing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a listening quiz on musical forms.

objectives: Compose and document an ABA composition

days.title: Motifs
days.work: Improvise and record five short motifs on your instrument or Song Maker.

days.title: Section A
days.work: Compose an 8-measure A section that expresses a chosen mood.

days.title: Section B
days.work: Compose a contrasting B section that changes rhythm, register or dynamics.

days.title: Notate
days.work: Write the composition in standard notation or save it in Song Maker.

days.title: Peer feedback
days.work: Play your draft for a listener and record their feedback using criteria.

weeks.topic: Music and other arts: film scoring
objectives: Connect music to film and storytelling
materials: silent film clip (e.g., Charlie Chaplin, public domain)

days.title: Film scores
days.work: Watch a film scene with and without sound and describe how music changes the meaning.

days.title: Leitmotif
days.work: Identify leitmotifs in a film score example and create a leitmotif for a character.

days.title: Score a scene
days.work: Create music or sound effects to accompany a short public-domain silent film clip.

days.title: Final composition
days.work: Revise your ABA composition and perform or play back the final version.

days.title: Review & critique
days.work: Evaluate your composition and film score with criteria and write a reflection.

weeks.assessment: Final composition and film score presentation.

days.title: Warm-ups
days.work: Do vocal and physical warm-ups (tongue twisters, mirror game) and learn theatre etiquette.

days.title: Yes, and
days.work: Play 'Yes, and' storytelling and 'Freeze' improv with family members.

days.title: Objectives
days.work: Improvise scenes where each character wants something different and identify the objective.

days.title: Tableaux
days.work: Create frozen tableaux of three moments from a myth studied in history.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Write about what made an improv scene work and what you would change.

objectives: Use vocal and physical choices to create character

days.title: Vocal choices
days.work: Read one line in 6 different emotions and change pitch, pace and volume.

days.title: Physical choices
days.work: Walk as different characters (king, child, old sailor) leading with different body parts.

days.title: Character profile
days.work: Choose a monologue and write a character profile (age, wants, fears, inner thoughts).

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Memorize and rehearse the monologue with blocking.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform the monologue and record personal reactions to your choices.

weeks.topic: Adapting a story for the stage
objectives: Identify essential events in a story
Adapt a story into a script
materials: Aesop's fable or Greek myth text

days.title: Essential events
days.work: Choose a fable or myth and identify the essential events that make up its dramatic structure.

days.title: Scripting
days.work: Write a 2-3 page script with dialogue and stage directions.

days.title: Staging problems
days.work: Solve staging challenges (a flying horse, a storm) with simple props, sound or movement.

days.title: Table read
days.work: Do a table read with family and revise the script based on what did not work.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Finalize the script and plan props and costumes.

objectives: Rehearse and present an adapted play

days.title: Blocking
days.work: Block the play: mark entrances, exits and positions.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse with scripts, then off book for the first half.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Hold a dress rehearsal with costumes and props.

days.title: Performance
days.work: Perform the play for an audience and record it.

days.title: Response
days.work: Watch the recording and write a critique of artistic choices using theatre vocabulary.

objectives: Apply rule of thirds, leading lines and framing

days.title: Composition rules
days.work: Study example photos for rule of thirds, leading lines and framing.

days.title: Rule of thirds
days.work: Take 10 photos using the rule-of-thirds grid and choose the best two.

days.title: Angles
days.work: Photograph the same object from bird's-eye, eye-level and worm's-eye views.

days.title: Photo walk
days.work: Take a neighborhood photo walk and capture leading lines, patterns and textures.

days.title: Review & critique
days.work: Select your best 5 photos and explain the composition technique in each.

objectives: Sequence photos to tell a story

days.title: Visual storytelling
days.work: Analyze a photo essay and identify beginning, middle and end.

days.title: Storyboard
days.work: Storyboard a 6-photo story about a family routine or recipe.

days.title: Shoot
days.work: Take the photos following your storyboard.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Crop and adjust contrast; discuss when photo editing becomes misleading manipulation.

days.title: Review & share
days.work: Present your photo story and gather feedback.

days.title: Flip book
days.work: Make a 20-page flip book of a bouncing ball on sticky notes.

days.title: Animation history
days.work: Watch early animation (zoetrope, Muybridge's horse) and explain persistence of vision.

days.title: Story idea
days.work: Develop a 20-30 second animation idea with a character, problem and solution.

days.title: Storyboard
days.work: Draw an 8-panel storyboard with camera angles.

days.title: Build set
days.work: Build characters and a simple set from clay or LEGO.

objectives: Shoot and edit a stop-motion animation

days.title: Test shots
days.work: Shoot a 2-second test and adjust lighting and camera stability.

days.title: Shoot part 1
days.work: Shoot the first half of the animation, moving figures in small increments.

days.title: Shoot part 2
days.work: Shoot the second half.

days.title: Edit and sound
days.work: Edit timing, add titles, credits and sound or music.

days.title: Screening
days.work: Screen the animation for your family and reflect on what you would improve.

weeks.topic: Elements of dance and cultural dance
objectives: Use body, energy, space and time in movement
Interpret the cultural meaning of dances

days.title: Elements of dance
days.work: Explore levels, pathways and energy by moving across the room in 10 different ways.

days.title: Greek folk dance
days.work: Learn a basic Greek line dance (e.g., Kalamatianos steps) from a video.

days.title: Mexican folk dance
days.work: Learn the basic zapateado step from ballet folklorico and discuss its regional origin.

days.title: Indian dance
days.work: Watch a Bharatanatyam excerpt and try three hand gestures (mudras) that tell a story.

days.title: Review & reflect
days.work: Write how one dance communicates its community's history or purpose.

objectives: Choreograph a short dance from a stimulus
materials: poem or natural phenomenon as inspiration

days.title: Stimulus
days.work: Choose a stimulus (a poem, the water cycle, a storm) and brainstorm movements.

days.title: Motifs
days.work: Create three movement motifs and vary them in level and speed.

days.title: Structure
days.work: Arrange motifs into a 1-minute dance with a beginning, middle and end.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse with a partner using unison and canon.

days.title: Perform
days.work: Perform and record the dance, then explain how it connects to the stimulus.

days.title: Big idea
days.work: Review your sketchbook ideas page and choose a personally meaningful theme.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Make three thumbnail sketches and choose media.

days.title: Create
days.work: Begin the culminating artwork.

days.title: Create and revise
days.work: Continue the artwork and get feedback halfway through.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Complete the artwork and reflect on whether it conveys your intended meaning.

objectives: Evaluate how museums reflect community values

days.title: Museum visit
days.work: Visit a local or virtual museum (e.g., the Getty or LACMA online) and note how works are grouped and labeled.

days.title: Community values
days.work: Write how the museum's choices reflect its community's history and values.

days.title: Select works
days.work: Select 8-10 of your works from the year across visual art and media arts.

days.title: Display plan
days.work: Draw a display plan for your exhibition showing placement and flow.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share the plan and revise based on feedback.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write a one-paragraph artist statement about your growth and interests.

days.title: Wall labels
days.work: Write wall labels (title, media, year, one sentence) for each piece.

days.title: Mat and mount
days.work: Mat and mount 2D works and prepare stands for 3D works.

days.title: Digital portfolio
days.work: Photograph all works and assemble a digital portfolio including your animation and music recordings.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Evaluate portfolio completeness with a checklist.

days.title: Install
days.work: Install your exhibition following your display plan.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse a short music performance and dance or monologue for the showcase.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Host the showcase: guide visitors as a docent and perform.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Collect written comments from visitors and summarize them.

days.title: Final reflection
days.work: Write a final reflection on your favorite project and set an arts goal for grade 7.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: Physical Education 6
courses.description: Grade 6 PE emphasizes working cooperatively toward common goals while refining skills in invasion, net/wall, striking/fielding, rhythmic and individual activities. Students learn fitness concepts (FITT, heart-rate zones, components of health-related fitness), take FITNESSGRAM-style baseline and end-of-year assessments, and build a personal fitness plan. Lessons are designed for a backyard, park or co-op with minimal equipment; every day includes a warm-up and at least 20 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity.
courses.framework: Physical Education Model Content Standards for California Public Schools (Grade 6); 2009 CA Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-6.1.1: Throw, kick and strike objects with accuracy and appropriate force using mature form in cooperative and individual activities.
standards.PE-6.1.2: Combine locomotor, non-locomotor and manipulative skills to work cooperatively toward a common goal.
standards.PE-6.1.3: Perform rhythmic patterns and folk, line and cooperative dances with accuracy and coordination.
standards.PE-6.1.4: Demonstrate mature technique for dribbling, passing, volleying, setting and receiving in game settings.
standards.PE-6.2.1: Explain how to modify skills and strategies to work effectively with a partner or team.
standards.PE-6.2.2: Use practice, feedback and critical elements to analyze and improve one's own and others' skill performance.
standards.PE-6.2.3: Explain and apply basic offensive and defensive strategies in cooperative, invasion, net and fielding games.
standards.PE-6.3.1: Participate in moderate to vigorous physical activity a minimum of four days each week, and track activity.
standards.PE-6.3.2: Assess aerobic capacity, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility and body composition using a standard fitness test.
standards.PE-6.3.3: Set and monitor short- and long-term goals to improve health-related fitness.
standards.PE-6.4.1: Explain and apply the FITT principles (frequency, intensity, time, type) to a personal fitness plan.
standards.PE-6.4.2: Measure heart rate and explain target heart-rate zones and recovery.
standards.PE-6.4.3: Explain the purpose of warm-up and cool-down, safe practices, hydration and nutrition for activity.
standards.PE-6.5.1: Cooperate with others, communicate positively and accept roles to accomplish a group goal.
standards.PE-6.5.2: Demonstrate responsible behavior, sportsmanship and conflict-resolution skills during activity.
standards.PE-6.5.3: Include and encourage others of different skill levels and abilities.

units.title: Fitness Baseline and Goal Setting
units.big_idea: Knowing your current fitness lets you set meaningful goals and train safely.

units.title: Cooperative Challenges and Team Building
units.big_idea: Teams succeed when members communicate, plan together and include everyone.

units.title: Invasion Games: Soccer and Ultimate
units.big_idea: Invasion games share strategies: create space on offense, deny space on defense.

units.title: Invasion Games: Basketball
units.big_idea: Ball control, passing and spacing make team offense effective.

units.big_idea: Net games reward controlled contacts and placing the object where opponents are not.

objectives: Perform a dynamic warm-up and cool-down
Measure resting and active heart rate

days.title: Dynamic warm-up
days.work: Learn a 10-move dynamic warm-up (high knees, butt kicks, carioca, arm circles) and a static-stretch cool-down.

days.title: Finding your pulse
days.work: Find your carotid and radial pulse, measure resting heart rate for 15 seconds x 4, and record it.

days.title: Heart rate response
days.work: Measure heart rate after walking, jogging and sprinting for 1 minute each and graph the results.

days.title: Safety and hydration
days.work: Play a tag game, then discuss heat safety, hydration and proper shoes; set a daily water goal.

days.title: Check
days.work: Lead the warm-up yourself and complete a short quiz on heart rate and warm-up purpose.

weeks.topic: Fitness testing: aerobic capacity and strength
materials: PACER audio (free online) or measured 20 m course

days.title: PACER or mile
days.work: Complete the 20-meter PACER test or a timed one-mile run/walk and record laps or time.

days.title: Curl-ups
days.work: Learn correct curl-up form and complete the cadence curl-up test.

days.title: Push-ups
days.work: Learn 90-degree push-up form and complete the cadence push-up test.

days.title: Active recovery
days.work: Play a low-intensity game (frisbee catch) and record test results in a fitness log.

days.title: Check
days.work: Compare your results with the Healthy Fitness Zone charts for your age.

weeks.topic: Fitness testing: flexibility and goal setting

days.title: Sit-and-reach
days.work: Complete the back-saver sit-and-reach test on both legs.

days.title: Trunk lift
days.work: Complete the trunk-lift test and learn safe back-strengthening exercises.

days.title: Components of fitness
days.work: Learn the five components of health-related fitness and match each test to a component; play a circuit game.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Write two SMART goals based on your baseline results.

days.title: Check
days.work: Share goals with a parent and do a 20-minute circuit targeting your goal areas.

objectives: Communicate clearly to solve group problems

days.title: Blindfold maze
days.work: Guide a blindfolded partner through a cone maze using only verbal directions, then switch.

days.title: Hula hoop pass
days.work: Pass a hula hoop around a hand-holding circle without letting go; time and improve.

days.title: Human knot
days.work: Untangle a human knot with family or co-op members and discuss communication strategies.

days.title: Encouragement game
days.work: Play a relay where teams earn points for encouraging words as well as speed.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write about one way you helped your team and one way to improve.

objectives: Plan and test strategies as a group

days.title: Lava river

days.title: Group juggle
days.work: Pass several balls in a set pattern around a circle and add balls as success grows.

days.title: Keep it up
days.work: Keep a balloon or beach ball in the air as long as possible with each person touching it in order.

days.title: Modify for all
days.work: Redesign one challenge so a person using a wheelchair or with limited vision could fully take part.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Record your group's best times and explain which strategy change helped most.

days.title: Sheet games
days.work: Play bedsheet or parachute games (popcorn, mushroom) that require timing together.

days.title: Cooperative tag
days.work: Play 'everybody's it' and 'freeze tag with rescue' and track steps.

days.title: Team circuit
days.work: Complete a partner fitness circuit where partners must sync reps.

days.title: Design a game
days.work: Design a cooperative game with rules and teach it to family members.

days.title: Check
days.work: Play your designed game and evaluate it for activity level and inclusion.

objectives: Dribble with control using inside and outside of foot
Pass accurately with the inside of the foot

days.title: Dribbling
days.work: Dribble through a cone course using inside, outside and sole touches.

days.title: Passing
days.work: Practice inside-foot passes with a partner or against a wall at 5 and 10 meters.

days.title: Receiving
days.work: Trap balls with the inside of the foot and thigh, then pass in one motion.

days.title: Small-sided game
days.work: Play 2v1 keep-away to practice passing into open space.

days.title: Skill check
days.work: Complete a skill check: 10 passes through a 1-meter cone gate and a timed dribble course.

objectives: Apply spacing and support in small games

days.title: Shooting
days.work: Practice instep shots at a target from 10 meters, aiming for the corners.

days.title: Offensive spacing
days.work: Learn to create passing triangles and move to open space in a 3v1 drill.

days.title: Defense
days.work: Practice defensive stance, jockeying and staying goal-side.

days.title: Game day
days.work: Play small-sided soccer, rotating positions and practicing fair play.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write about one offensive and one defensive strategy you used.

weeks.topic: Ultimate: throwing and catching a disc
objectives: Catch with pancake and rim catches

days.work: Practice backhand throws to a partner, focusing on a flat release.

days.title: Catching
days.work: Practice pancake and rim catches at different heights.

days.title: Forehand

days.title: Pivot and pass
days.work: Practice pivoting to avoid a marker and passing to a moving receiver.

days.title: Skill check
days.work: Complete 10 backhand throws to a target 10 meters away and record successes.

weeks.topic: Ultimate: game play and Spirit of the Game
objectives: Play ultimate using rules and self-officiating

days.work: Learn ultimate rules and practice a stall count while marking.

days.title: Cutting
days.work: Practice cuts to get open and the 'give and go'.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play ultimate, resolving calls through Spirit of the Game discussion.

days.title: Compare strategies
days.work: Compare soccer and ultimate strategies on a chart and play a modified game.

days.title: Unit check
days.work: Take a quiz on invasion strategies and self-assess sportsmanship.

days.title: Ball handling
days.work: Complete ball-handling drills (around the waist, figure 8, finger taps).

days.title: Dribbling
days.work: Practice control and speed dribbles with each hand through cones.

days.title: Crossover
days.work: Learn the crossover dribble and practice it against a partner defender.

days.title: Peer feedback
days.work: Use a critical-elements checklist to give a partner feedback on dribbling.

days.title: Skill check
days.work: Complete a timed dribble course with both hands.

days.work: Practice chest, bounce and overhead passes to a wall target, 20 each.

days.title: Shooting form

days.title: Layups

courses.subject: HEALTH
courses.title: Health 6
courses.description: Grade 6 health education aligned to the 2008 California Health Education Content Standards, which focus sixth grade on Mental, Emotional and Social Health; Injury Prevention and Safety; and Personal and Community Health. Students learn to identify emotions, manage stress, build self-esteem, communicate assertively, resolve conflict, prevent bullying and stay safe online, and recognize when to seek mental-health help. They then practice injury prevention, first aid, 911 calls and California earthquake/wildfire preparedness, study disease prevention, immunity and consumer health, and finish with a community health advocacy project.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a home safety action plan and complete a check.

days.title: Water safety
days.work: Learn about drowning prevention, rip currents and life-jacket fit for pools, lakes and beaches.

days.title: Concussions
days.work: Read about concussion signs and why to stop playing and tell an adult.

days.title: Protective gear
days.work: Inspect sports gear and check helmet fit using the 2-V-1 rule.

days.title: Heat illness
days.work: Learn signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke and prevention steps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a sports safety checklist and take a quiz.

days.title: Road rules
days.work: Learn CA rules for cyclists and pedestrians, including helmet law under 18.

days.title: Bike check
days.work: Do an ABC quick check (air, brakes, chain) and ride a safe route with a parent.

days.title: Distractions
days.work: Discuss phone and headphone distraction while walking or riding.

days.title: Risk influences
days.work: Analyze stunt videos and peer dares that encourage risky behavior.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Map a safe route to a local destination and explain hazards.

objectives: Treat minor wounds, burns and nosebleeds

days.title: Check-Call-Care
days.work: Learn the Check-Call-Care steps and practice scene safety checks.

days.title: Bleeding
days.work: Practice direct pressure and bandaging on a family member with gloves.

days.title: Burns
days.work: Learn first aid for minor burns (cool water, cover) and when to get help.

days.title: Nosebleeds and sprains
days.work: Practice nosebleed care and RICE for sprains.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Inventory and restock the home first aid kit and complete a skills check.

objectives: Respond to choking and allergic reactions

days.title: Choking
days.work: Learn signs of choking and practice abdominal-thrust hand position on a pillow (no thrusts on people).

days.title: Allergic reactions
days.work: Learn signs of anaphylaxis and how an epinephrine auto-injector trainer is used.

days.title: Hands-only CPR intro
days.work: Watch an American Heart Association Hands-Only CPR video and practice compression rhythm on a pillow.

days.title: 911 or not?
days.work: Decide in 10 scenarios whether to call 911, call a parent, or give first aid.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Injury Prevention and First Aid unit test.

days.title: 911 calls
days.work: Learn what dispatchers ask and practice a mock 911 call with a parent playing dispatcher.

days.title: Know your info
days.work: Memorize your address and parents' numbers and set up an ICE contact.

days.title: Local resources
days.work: Locate nearest fire station, hospital and police station on a map.

days.title: Home alone safety
days.work: Write home-alone rules with a parent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a mock-call rubric and contact card.

objectives: Practice drop, cover and hold on

days.title: Earthquake science
days.work: Review why California has earthquakes and what to do indoors, outdoors and in a car.

days.title: Drill
days.work: Practice Drop, Cover and Hold On in 3 rooms and identify safe spots.

days.title: Fire escape plan
days.work: Draw a home floor plan with two exits from each room and a meeting place.

days.title: Fire drill
days.work: Run a family fire drill and time it; practice stop, drop and roll and crawling low.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer a quiz on earthquake and fire safety.

days.title: Wildfire and smoke
days.work: Learn evacuation zones and how to read the Air Quality Index during wildfire smoke.

days.title: Go-bag
days.work: Pack or list a 72-hour go-bag using the Ready.gov checklist.

days.title: Family plan
days.work: Complete a family communication plan with an out-of-area contact.

days.title: Help others
days.work: Plan how to help a neighbor, pet or elderly relative in an emergency.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the family emergency plan and take the Preparedness unit quiz.

objectives: Describe dangers of weapons and gangs

days.title: Types of violence
days.work: Discuss physical, verbal and emotional violence and their effects.

days.title: Warning signs
days.work: List warning signs of potential violence and why to tell an adult.

days.title: Weapons
days.work: Learn the rule if you see a gun: don't touch, leave, tell an adult.

days.title: Gangs
days.work: Read about gang recruitment and list positive alternatives.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Role-play de-escalating a heated argument; complete a check.

days.title: Trust your gut
days.work: Discuss intuition and practice identifying uh-oh feelings in scenarios.

days.title: Boundaries
days.work: Learn personal-boundary rights and practice saying no to unwanted touch or requests.

days.title: Grooming warning signs
days.work: Learn warning signs such as secrets, gifts and isolation from adults or online contacts.

days.title: Escape plan
days.work: Practice No-Go-Tell and create a code word with your family.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Violence Prevention and Personal Safety unit quiz.

weeks.topic: Personal hygiene and dental care for adolescents

days.title: Hygiene review
days.work: Review skin, hair and body odor care and update your hygiene routine for middle school.

days.title: Acne myths
days.work: Sort acne myths and facts using KidsHealth and plan a gentle skin routine.

days.title: Dental health
days.work: Learn about gingivitis and practice proper flossing.

days.title: Sports hygiene
days.work: List hygiene rules for sports gear, showers and preventing athlete's foot.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a hygiene self-assessment and quiz.

days.title: Sleep needs
days.work: Learn why 9–12 hours matter for preteens and keep a 3-night sleep log.

days.title: Screens and sleep
days.work: Discuss blue light and phones in bedrooms and plan a device curfew.

days.title: Hearing
days.work: Use a sound meter app to measure common noises and learn safe headphone volume (60/60 rule).

days.title: Sun and eyes
days.work: Read a sunscreen label, check the UV index and learn the 20-20-20 eye rule.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a personal health practice goal and take a quiz.

weeks.topic: Communicable diseases and the immune system

days.title: Pathogens
days.work: Compare bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa and give a disease example for each.

days.title: How germs spread
days.work: Model germ spread with glitter on hands and objects around the house.

days.title: Handwashing test
days.work: Test glitter removal with water only vs. 20-second soap wash and record results.

days.title: Immune defenses
days.work: Draw the body's lines of defense (skin, mucus, white blood cells, antibodies) and explain how vaccines work.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a communicable disease quiz.

days.title: Chronic diseases
days.work: Research one chronic disease (asthma, diabetes, heart disease, cancer) and make a fact card.

days.title: Asthma
days.work: Learn asthma triggers and how an inhaler helps; discuss how to help a friend having an attack.

days.title: Risk factors
days.work: Sort controllable and uncontrollable risk factors for chronic disease.

days.title: Family history
days.work: Complete a simple family health history with a parent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on habits that lower chronic disease risk; complete a check.

days.title: Ad claims
days.work: Analyze 4 health-product ads for claims, techniques and missing information.

days.title: Comparison shopping
days.work: Compare name-brand and generic versions of a product by ingredients and unit price.

days.title: Quackery
days.work: Identify red flags of health fraud (miracle cure, secret formula, testimonials only).

days.title: Decide
days.work: Use DECIDE to choose a sunscreen or toothpaste and justify the choice.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a consumer-health worksheet.

days.title: Providers
days.work: Match 10 health-care providers to what they do.

days.title: Check-up prep
days.work: Write questions to ask at your next check-up and learn what a well-child visit includes.

days.title: Pharmacist role
days.work: Read a prescription label and list questions to ask a pharmacist.

days.title: Community services
days.work: Locate a local clinic, dentist and public health department online.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Personal and Consumer Health unit test.

days.title: Air quality
days.work: Check the local AQI for a week and graph it.

days.title: Water and noise
days.work: Learn about safe drinking water and noise pollution in your community.

days.title: Trash audit
days.work: Conduct a one-day household trash audit and plan reduce/reuse/recycle steps.

days.title: Public health
days.work: Research what your county public health department does.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Choose a community health issue for your advocacy project and justify it.

objectives: Plan and create an advocacy project

days.title: Research
days.work: Gather 4 facts from valid sources about your chosen issue (kindness, emergency preparedness, sun safety, clean air).

days.title: Plan
days.work: Identify audience, message and call to action.

days.title: Create
days.work: Produce a poster, brochure, slide show or short video.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Practice a 3-minute presentation and get feedback.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Revise using an advocacy rubric.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present your advocacy project to family, co-op or a community group.

days.title: Review game
days.work: Play a review game on mental health, safety and personal health.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year health assessment.

days.title: Goal review
days.work: Review your wellness wheel from week 1 and re-rate each area.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on your growth and a summer health and safety plan.
